emulators.name: DOSBox Wii
emulators.description: DOSBox 的 GameCube 与 Wii 移植。
emulators.latest_body: * **Start straight into a game (Wii).** Name a game when you launch DOSBox Wii and it starts with that game's config on top of `dosbox.conf`: from the Homebrew Channel (`<arguments>` in `meta.xml`) or from WiiFlow, either as a plugin (the zip now includes `wiiflow/plugins/dosbox-wii.ini`, which lists the `.conf` files in `DOSBox/Games` as games) or from its Homebrew list. A game can be named as `-gameconf <conf or folder>`, as a bare `.conf`, or as a bare folder that holds one (`autoboot.conf`, or its only `.conf`). A relative name is looked for as written, beside the launched `boot.dol`, then in the `DOSBox` folder, so a game's `.conf`, `.map` and files can all live in one folder, anywhere. If the game cannot be found DOSBox starts without one and says why on the DOS screen. The **Status** page has an **Autoboot** row, and the app now knows it was started this way (`IsAutoboot()`), ready for a single-game menu later. See the README's *Starting a game at launch*

## 4.0.4 - November 3, 2026
* **The left analog stick now moves the pointer in the menus**, on every controller, like a mouse. It no longer also steps through the buttons; the D-pad still does
* **A Wiimote with anything plugged into it is now always vertical in the menus**, and its buttons and IR pointer work alongside the extension (a Nunchuk on Wii and a Classic Controller on both Wii and Wii U previously lost them)
* **Redesigned Button Mappings screen.** One screen now replaces the separate controller and button screens, showing each button on a drawing of the controller and letting you choose a button by pressing it or from a list.

Snapshots fill a grid, with the game's **Cartridge Save** (shown only for games that have one) in its own card beneath. Choosing a card opens a small popover of what can be done with it; the save file's backups are listed from its popover. The Auto Load, Auto Save and Append Auto settings are replaced by a single **Save Mode**: **Snapshot** (the default), **Cartridge Save**, or **Manual**.

releases.name: 4.0.3 - October 20, 2026
releases.body:
* **New menu look!** The menus have been rebuilt with a fresh, modern style: a deeper red header and footer, cleaner rounded buttons with soft shadows, a redesigned game list with a slimmer scrollbar and a clear highlight on the selected entry, new prompt windows, and more. The menu graphics are now drawn procedurally by the renderer instead of being loaded from PNG images, so they stay sharp at any output resolution
* **New controller status bar** in the menu footer, replacing the Wiimote battery icons. * Wii U: fix texture reuse causing cover art issues with varying image sizes

Each of the four player slots (P1-P4) now shows the type of controller connected (Wiimote, GameCube controller, etc.), with the battery level shown for Wiimote controllers and the Gamepad. Empty slots appear dimmed
* Wii U: the Wiimote tilt sensor now works (Kirby Tilt-N-Tumble, Yoshi Topsy-Turvy, WarioWare Twisted!, Boktai's Gun Del Sol), and Yoshi's Universal Gravitation rotates the screen as on Wii
* Wii U: Japanese/Korean/Chinese fonts are now also found in `vbagx/` or `wiiu/apps/vbagx/` on the SD card even before settings have been saved, and stay crisp at 1080p
* Wii U: fix texture reuse causing cover art issues with varying image sizes
* Wii U: fix aspect ratio issues

## Enhancements

- The floppy disk API now supports disk images stored in memory buffers (#992)
- Added proper gamma correction to the palette builders (#998)

## Bug Fixes

Changes since the latest beta release:

releases.body:
Changes since the latest beta release:
- Fixed two UI issues (#843, #846)
- Fixed a bug in the CBM file system implementation (#853)
- Fixed a bug in the drive idle logic (#854)
- Fixed three drive-related VICE tests (#668, #674, #675)

Core and API

* Public API: The API now has as new shape. There are async counterparts (…Async) for state-changing calls, set is now setAsync, there is a new MemoryDebugger API, more getters, and suspend/resume coverage across the API.
* Threading: The command queue and message queue are now std::deque-based. Messages can carry exceptions. AudioPort is thread-safe. Cmd::CALL, TRACK_ON and TRACK_OFF are new.
* Messages: Msg::CONFIG is sent for every option change. ROM_LOADED, RSH_DONE and CONFIG_ERROR are new.
* RetroShell: It has the new architecture from vAmiga, with multiple shells and a single console per shell.
* Workspaces: A screenshot is now saved inside saveWorkspace().
* X-Ray: GPU X-Ray support is added, with a new XRAY_COMPOSITOR option.
* Shared libraries: utlib and rvlib were merged with the versions shared with vAmiga and Silicium.
* Cleanup: Header, include and namespace cleanups, plus removal of orphaned files.

Fixes

* Drive::isIdle() is fixed (#854).

This maintenance release primarily addresses issue #851, which prevented the app from running on the upcoming macOS 27 Golden Gate. It also includes internal code changes required to make the core compatible with the architecture of the upcoming Silicium emulator.
Removing beta status, as no significant bugs have been reported for some time.

## Refactoring

This beta release introduces substantial changes to the underlying code base. As part of the development of the RetroVault app, a new **RetroVault** library has been created. This library is now responsible for managing:

- File systems  
- Devices  
- All supported image formats  

RetroVault is designed as a standalone library and is also used in the latest version of vAmiga for the same purpose.

In addition, the new **utlib** library has been introduced. All utility functions previously embedded in vAmiga and VirtualC64 have been refactored into this more powerful shared library. This makes it easier for me to share common functionality among the different emulators. 

## Enhancements

- The disassembler now supports symbol files (#837)

## Bug Fixes

## DK64 Recompiled — APK Android 1.0.3-android

APK **release assinado** (arm64-v8a), compilado pelo workflow `release` no commit `7edb0f7` (`fix/first-launch-crash`).

---

## O que mudou nesta branch (`fix/first-launch-crash`)

### Corrigido o crash na 1ª inicialização (selecionar ROM + Start Game fechava o app)
Na primeira execução do app, depois de selecionar a ROM e tocar em **Start Game**, o app fechava sozinho; na segunda inicialização funcionava perfeitamente. Causa raiz multi-fator, todas eliminadas:

- **Ciclo do seletor de ROM quebrava a sessão gráfica**: ao abrir o seletor (DocumentsUI), a surface Vulkan era destruída/recriada e a fila de present ficava congelada — o **Start Game** na MESMA sessão rodava em estado frágil (por isso o processo limpo da 2ª execução funcionava). Agora, após a ROM ser selecionada, **o app reinicia sozinho** (~1,5 s, o mesmo mecanismo do menu de GPU Driver) e o Start Game roda num processo limpo, com a Vulkan inicializada apenas 1× por processo.

releases.body:
## Novidades — 1.0.3-android

Resumo do que foi feito nos commits da branch `fix/mod-file-picker-saf`:

### 🎮 Gamepad virtual — redesign completo ("dark glass" + identidade N64)
- Novo visual em **vidro escuro** com gradientes, sombras suaves e contornos finos — fim dos halos planos.
- **Identidade de cor por botão** como no hardware do N64: A azul, B verde, C amarelo, START vermelho; botões neutros acendem no verde-banana do DK64 ao serem pressionados.
- Feedback de toque com qualidade: o botão **afunda** e acende com glow radial, animações suaves de pressionar/soltar e o HUD entra/sai com fade + deslize.
- **Ergonomia**: áreas de toque generosas com prioridade por proximidade, histerese de saída (deslizar o dedo para fora solta o botão — mata "ghost press"), stick com zona morta reescalada, retorno animado do knob e menor latência de toque.
- **Correções de robustez**: o pad aparece sozinho quando o jogo inicia e reaparece se a Activity for recriada (novo acesso nativo `is_game_started`); controles respeitam a área do recorte (cutout) da tela; a escolha de esconder o HUD fica salva.

releases.name: DolphinVR Redux v0.5 - The Fall Update
releases.body:
DolphinVR Redux v0.5 brings VR game patches, which put your hands and your head into the games themselves, an in-game menu you use without taking the headset off, a large round of Meta Quest performance work, and automatic updates on Windows.

## Highlights

- **VR game patches.** The arm cannon follows your controller in the Metroid Prime games, the gun and sword follow it in Red Steel 1 and 2, Skyward Sword reads your controller's true pose, and Twilight Princess, The Wind Waker, Wii Sports and Shadow the Hedgehog can be played in first person.
- **An in-game VR menu.** Click the left thumbstick during a game to pause, fast forward, change settings, rebind controls, manage savestates and hunt overrides, all inside the headset.
- **Faster on Meta Quest.** Super Mario Galaxy went from 42 to 60 fps and Super Mario Sunshine from 49 to 60 fps at native resolution in my tests with "Smart Foveation EFB".
- **Automatic updates on Windows.** This is the first version that updates itself. See "Installing" below.
- **Rebased on the latest Dolphin** development builds (October 2026).

## VR game patches

releases.name: DolphinVR Redux v0.4 — The Summer Update
releases.body:
DolphinVR Redux v0.4 introduces new graphics backends, major OpenXR improvements, Meta Quest passthrough support, expanded VR configuration tools, and a wide range of rendering and stability fixes.

Highlights

- Added DirectX 12 and OpenGL renderer support.
- Added OpenXR asynchronous mode for Vulkan and DirectX 12.
- Added passthrough support for Meta Quest headsets.
- Added foveated rendering to improve performance on Quest.
- Introduced a new VR configuration panel for binding controls directly in VR.
- Improved the Texture Override, Hide Code, and Shader Hunter tools.


OpenXR and VR

- Added OpenXR asynchronous mode for Vulkan and DirectX 12.
- Added an eager frame heartbeat for native VR frame-rate operation.
- Added a new VR configuration panel for controller bindings.
- Added new camera and controller anchor overrides.
- Added a new "Screen pane" override.
- Updated the Wiimote pointer to use absolute pointing.
- Fixed Wii MotionPlus gyroscope behavior.

Meta Quest

- Added passthrough support for Meta Quest headsets.
- Added foveated rendering to improve performance.
- Added a new first-launch screen for applying recommended Quest bindings.

releases.name: Dolphin VR Redux v0.3 — The Metroid Update
releases.body:
This update brings a major round of improvements, with a strong focus on Metroid Prime, element overrides, Vulkan rendering, and overall performance.

- All major Metroid Prime fixes from the 2016 DolphinVR-Hydra branch have now been ported and integrated, including: Detect Skybox, Remove Cinematic Bars, 3D HUD, Visor EFB Skips...

- These fixes have also been improved with additional work, such as the Layered Palette Conversion Path, which restores the thermal, X-Ray, dark, and scanner visor effects in Metroid Prime 1, 2, and 3

- Added Headlock HUD support for Metroid Prime Trilogy

- Fixed the Element Override Tool, which can now finally work with projection-based definition overrides

- Added a new Texture Element Override system that, unlike shader-based overrides, uses the texture hash to identify elements. It is easier to use and should remain persistent across versions

- Updated Vulkan with new fixes; it now uses full projection for every headset

- Improved performance through multiple bug fixes.

- Also includes an experimental release for Meta Quest 3 and Debian Linux

releases.name: Dolphin VR Redux v0.2 - Hotfix inputs
releases.body:
Removed /input/trigger/click and /input/squeeze/click from Oculus/Meta profiles that don't support them
Added FOCUSED session state tracking

releases.name: Dolphin VR Redux v0.2
releases.body:
- Improved VR controller support
- Added a VR input tester scene for OpenXR Wii Remote configuration when no game is running
- Updated the VR settings panel
- Added initial AR mode support by Clodo76
- Added a work-in-progress culling code finder
- Improved the Elements Hunting tool
- Force Immediately Present XFB is now disabled by default, with a new OpenXR toggle available
- Added a new Lock Head Pose Per Frame option for games that do not work properly with Immediately Present XFB, such as Zack & Wiki

releases.name: DOSBox Pure 1.0 Preview 6
releases.body:
This is the sixth preview release of version 1.0 of DOSBox Pure.

A smaller update with additions and fixes. Again, please test this release and provide feedback as we work towards a release we can call 1.0. Feedback is welcome here on GitHub as well as on [Discord](https://discord.gg/swhZC8xFJw).

## New Features

### Support for Dynamic VHD Disk Images (#694)
Installing an operating system will also automatically create dynamic VHD files from now on (which initially is just a few megabytes and grows as needed)

### Volume Settings (93cf48b)
Volume settings were added to the core options for the various DOS devices (Sound Blaster, Adlib, MIDI, etc.)]

### Handle shut down requests in Windows 9x (#738)
Minimal implementation of APM (Advanced Power Management) BIOS functionality just to handle the power off request by Windows 9x. This will allow to automatically go back to the menu or exit the core/emulator when the emulated Windows is shut down.

## Minor Additions
- Allow mounting of ZIP files via IMGMOUNT command (with `IMGMOUNT X: file.zip -t zip`) (04a1b95)
- Support a custom extended M3U format tag to overlay the multiple contents (i.e. load multiple ZIP files as C:) (#731)

releases.name: DOSBox Pure 1.0 Preview 5
releases.body:
This is the fifth preview release of version 1.0 of DOSBox Pure.

A small update with a few fixes. Again, please test this release and provide feedback as we work towards a release we can call 1.0. Feedback is welcome here on GitHub as well as on [Discord](https://discord.gg/NY52DcUFgK).

## Changes
- Add mode "On (Only On-Screen Keyboard While in Game)" to "Use L3 Button to Show Menu" core input option (#715)
- Fix IDE CD-ROM and hard drive conflict causing a unnecessary delay during booting of an operating system (#689)
- Avoid a potential core crash when the content video mode changes and the on-screen mouse cursor becomes out of view (#686)
- Prevent mouse inputs being able to cause rare random page faults while booted into Windows 9x (489626f)
- Port CPU fixes (for JMP/CALL/RET) from DOSBox-X to prevent some crashes when running Win9x (795db3e)
- Fix DOS table media id for mounted IMG/IMA floppy disks (fixes certain game installers) (#703)
- Avoid the C: drive of a mounted ZIP archive reporting more free than total space (fixes certain game installers) (#702)
- Fix INT 21 FINDFIRST call used to match a FAT drive volume label which contains spaces (#709)

releases.name: DOSBox-X 2026.08.31 2026-09-01 08:45
releases.body:
2026.08.31:
  - Added support for mounting TeleDisk (.td0) floppy image files. (cimarronm)
  - Fixed prompting of working directory option (maron2000)
  - Relax sanity check of floppy image considering specially formatted disks
    (maron2000)
  - Disk sector I/O now returns typed INT 13h status codes instead of a
    catch-all error, and the INT 13h handler propagates the specific code
    (seek failed, controller failure, CRC/data error, etc.) into register
    AH on read/write errors rather than collapsing every failure to 0x04.
    Also fixes AH being left stale on write errors and a VFD fill-sector
    write that reported failure after succeeding. (cimarronm)
  - On non-MSC, only define MIN/MAX if not already defined (skitt)
  - Fixed FreeDOS XCOPY failed to copy files when destination directory was
    not specified (maron2000)
  - IMGMOUNT: Fixed a regression that didn't try loading IMGMAKE.IMG if no 
    image was specified (maron2000)
  - Fixed a build error when FFmpeg is upgraded to FFmpeg 9 (maron2000)
  - Fixed freeze when savestate flagged file not found (rebb)
  - Fixed capture and savestate directory locations (maron2000)

releases.name: DOSBox-X 2026.08.02 2026-08-02 21:30
releases.body:
2026.08.02
  - Debugger: normalize 16-bit segmented offsets for address display/lookup and
    avoid false "[illegal]" memory operand reports in AnalyzeInstruction()
    (cimarronm)
  - Fixed character rendering and mouse cursor display in DOS/V Japanese mode.
    (nanshiki)
  - Fixed build error of OSFREE release builds (maron2000)
  - Added floppy BPB sanity check, and rearranged existing floppy BPB check code
    (maron2000)
  - Fixed window resizing (OpenGL, SDL2) (misty7666)
  - Updated Nuked-OPL3-fast to v1.8-fast.3 (tgies)
  - Added support for nested subdirectories in Z drive (maron2000)
  - Added experimental "ethnet" command and protocol for NE2000 emulation. Instead
    of using the pcap promiscious mode, which doesn't work over Wi-fi, a client
    server setup can be configured to emulate a private lan between instances of
    DOSBox-X either on localhost or on the local area network. The ethnet command
    is deliberately built so that client and server set up is the same command
    structure as the "ipx" command used to set up an IPX network in DOSBox and
    DOSBox-X. (joncampbell123)
  - FAT driver performance improvements, at least for directory enumeration,

releases.name: DroidDeck-Mali v0.4.0-beta.1 (Build 45) — Beta
releases.body:
# DroidDeck-Mali v0.4.0-beta.1 (Build 45) — Beta

**Esta es una beta: no es una versión final.** Se instala encima de la build anterior sin
perder datos (runtime y Steam se conservan; misma firma). Probada en **POCO X6 Pro
(Dimensity 8300-Ultra, Mali-G615 MC6)**, y pensada para **cualquier dispositivo con GPU Mali CSF**.

---

## 🎮 Novedades respecto a la versión anterior

- **Los juegos ya se ejecutan.** Ya no se quedan en el logo. Aún pueden tener caídas de
  fps, pero son mucho más estables.
- **HUD personalizable (estilo Winlator).** El mando en pantalla se edita con **perfiles con
  nombre**: duplica, añade, elimina y cambia de perfil para cada juego. Cada control tiene
  **forma** (círculo, redondeado, cuadrado) y **tamaño del 40 % al 250 %**; el d-pad se
  separa en flechas al agrandarlo; el touchpad queda sin etiqueta; la barra superior se
  puede **ocultar** y recuperar; los controles ya colocados **no se mueven** al añadir
  otros, y todo se guarda automáticamente al soltar.
- **Joystick de cámara (ratón).** Control nuevo para juegos 3D: mantén pulsado fuera del
  centro y mueve la cámara. Cuanto más grande lo pongas, más rápido gira.

releases.name: DroidDeck Mali-G615 v0.3.2-exp1 (Build 44) — Experimental Public Release
releases.body:
## DroidDeck Mali-G615 — First Official Experimental Public Release (`v0.3.2-mali-g615-exp1`, Build 44)

This is the first public experimental release of the **DroidDeck-Mali** fork, bringing **SteamOS Gaming Mode (Gamescope + Big Picture)**, **KDE Plasma Desktop Mode**, and **Proton / FEX / WOWBox64 / DXVK** Windows game execution to **ARM Mali-G615 (Valhall v10)** Android devices (tested on **POCO X6 Pro / Dimensity 8300-Ultra, Mali-G615 MC6**).

---

### ⚠️ IMPORTANT: How to Download & Import the GPU Drivers / IMPORTANTE: Cómo descargar e importar los drivers GPU

> **DO NOT extract the driver `.zip` files and DO NOT pack them inside another `.zip`.**
> Each driver `.zip` attached below is already formatted as an individual DroidDeck driver package (`manifest.json` + `icd.json` + `.so`). Download the `.zip` file you want and select that `.zip` **directly** inside the DroidDeck app:
> **`Components` → `GPU drivers` → `Import`** (or `Components` → `GPU drivers` → `Advanced` → `Runtime driver` → `Import`).
>
> **NO descomprimas los archivos `.zip` de los drivers ni los metas dentro de otro `.zip`.**

releases.name: DroidDeck software Vulkan driver (lavapipe)
releases.body:
## DroidDeck software Vulkan driver - Mesa lavapipe 25.0.7-2+deb13u1

A Vulkan driver that rasterises on the CPU, to bring up a session with the Mali GPU
kept out of the guest entirely. Not for playing: a frame takes seconds.

- [DroidDeck-Software-Vulkan-lavapipe.zip](https://github.com/jdmg28/DroidDeck-Mali-G615/releases/download/software-mode-lavapipe/DroidDeck-Software-Vulkan-lavapipe.zip)
- [DroidDeck-Software-Vulkan-lavapipe.zip.sha256](https://github.com/jdmg28/DroidDeck-Mali-G615/releases/download/software-mode-lavapipe/DroidDeck-Software-Vulkan-lavapipe.zip.sha256)

**To use it:** install the APK from
[software-mode-latest](https://github.com/jdmg28/DroidDeck-Mali-G615/releases/tag/software-mode-latest),
then Components -> GPU drivers -> Advanced -> Runtime driver -> Import, and pick the zip.
GPU safety is Auto, which is software on a Mali device, so there is nothing else to set.

Measured before it was packaged: the runtime (`r9`) carries glibc
2.43, and this driver asks for `GLIBC_2.38`. The zip's
`meta.json` records both, with the checksum of every Debian package the zip is made of.

# Packages

## Targets

Each build is optimized for a specific architecture and uses a specific compiler.

- **aarch64/arm64**: For devices that use the armv8-a instruction set; e.g. Snapdragon X, all Android devices, and Apple Silicon Macs.
- **amd64**: For devices that use the amd64 (aka x86_64) instruction set; this is exclusively used by Intel and AMD CPUs and is only found on desktops.

## Changelog

This is the first anniversary of Eden's inception, on May 10, 2025. It has been quite a hectic journey thus far, from drama, to server nukes, to DMCAs, to sysadmin nightmares, to exotic hardware/OS ports, to constant threats from all angles. Yet still, we survive, with countless improvements, bug fixes, performance enhancements, features, and so much more to show for it.

Thank you all so, so much for the constant support in the face of continuous, unending challenges and difficulties. Here's to many more years of Eden, and for the time being, enjoy 0.2.0 as your anniversary gift!

You are encouraged to read the [detailed changelog](https://git.eden-emu.dev/eden-emu/eden/compare/v0.2.0-rc2...v0.2.0).

releases.name: Eden SX2A v0.2.2
releases.body:
Unofficial, experimental build. Not Eden, not supported by the Eden team. Written largely with an AI coding assistant (Claude), tested by hand on one phone.

## v0.2.2

- **Mario Kart World 1.0.0 is in game, with graphical glitches.** Its older SDK asks the GPU session for its address range with a different command, and sets a display output mode the emulator rejected; both are handled now. Expect about 6-10 FPS, a dark road and missing surfaces (some of its shaders are not supported yet), flickering frames during races, and possibly a GPU crash while a course loads.
- **Default resolution is 1x** (was 0.5x, which looked bad and did not help the frame rate). Existing installs that never changed the resolution get 1x too.
- **Loose Switch 2 games show up in the games list.** Add the folder that holds your dumps as a game folder and grant All files access; each game is listed once with its newest update. "Launch ExeFS game folder" still works.
- **Switch 2 readiness check** in Settings: shows what is missing (RAM, Android version, GPU driver, recommended settings, All files access, games, storage, battery setting) with buttons to fix it.
- Three more Switch 2 shader instruction forms

Unofficial, experimental build. Not Eden, not supported by the Eden team. Written largely with an AI coding assistant (Claude), tested by hand on one phone.

## v0.2.1

This version is rebuilt on [Eden-NS2](https://github.com/0x2593/Eden-NS2) (0x2593's Switch 2 fork of Eden) instead of Takoroka's eden-nx2. Eden-NS2 is more actively developed, so this fork can now merge its fixes as they come. The Android layer and the phone fixes from v0.2 were carried over.

- **Faster:** the GPU work for Switch 2 games now runs on two threads on phones too, and GPU-written command lists are flushed with one wait instead of one per page. DK Bananza draws about twice as many objects per second as before.

- **Turnip driver bundled:** on Adreno GPUs the app installs Mr. Purple's Turnip T30 and selects it on first start, unless you already picked a driver. The stock Qualcomm driver loses some draws in Switch 2 games (DK Bananza's ground).
- **Pokémon Pokopia is playable at about 20 FPS**, the best-running game so far. Fixed a crash when entering the game.
- DK Bananza's destructible te

emulators.name: EmuFive
emulators.description: 在越狱的 PlayStation 4 上通过 Linux 运行 PlayStation 5 游戏。
emulators.note: 仅限已越狱的 PlayStation 4。

releases.name: v1.0.12
releases.body:
## EmuFive 1.0.12: no more black screen with `emufive.mode=`

### What's new
- **Fixed: a black screen with `emufive.mode=` in `bootargs.txt`** (PS4 Multiboot #10). EmuFive set the TV's 1080p mode, then its home screen switched to another 1920x1080 mode (59.96 Hz, 173 MHz) that isn't one of the TV's modes, and some TVs show nothing with it. The home screen now keeps the mode EmuFive set. Checked on a PS4 Pro at 1080p and at 4K.

### Update
Settings, System, Software update. No restart needed: the home screen starts again by itself.

If your screen is black because of `emufive.mode=`, remove it from `bootargs.txt` first, update, then add it back.

From 1.0.3 or earlier, start the update once by hand (see the README's Changelog).

### New installs
Use the `ps5-ps4-rootfs.tar.xz` of this release.

releases.name: v1.0.11
releases.body:
## EmuFive 1.0.11: Teardown's large maps no longer close EmuFive

### What's new
- **Fixed: EmuFive closed with "unsupported buffer readback from an asynchronous GPU completion"** when GPU-shared memory was on (Teardown's large maps on a PS4 Slim, #21). When the GPU finishes work, EmuFive writes a "done" marker into the game's memory. When that page was write-protected, the write needed the GPU thread while it could be waiting for the writer. Such markers are now written by the GPU thread.
- **A new emulator build** (KytyPS5 589bd14 with EmuFive patches 0001–0035).

Large maps still load slowly when they fill the PS4's RAM.

### Update
Settings, System, Software update. No restart needed.

From 1.0.3 or earlier, start the update once by hand (see the README's Changelog).

### New installs
Use the `ps5-ps4-rootfs.tar.xz` of this release.

releases.name: v1.0.10
releases.body:
## EmuFive 1.0.10: cleaner 3D games, Wytchwood fix, screen mode

### What's new
- **No more white dashes and stale pixel blocks in 3D games** (Blue Prince). The PS4 GPU's colour fast clears and its depth and MSAA compression left 8×8-pixel blocks behind when a game read an image back; EmuFive now turns them off. Blue Prince is playable on a PS4 Pro at about 25 FPS.
- **Wytchwood: no more full-screen noise near objects you can interact with.** A new full-screen mask the game reads before drawing it held leftover bytes from other images; it now starts full. Wytchwood is playable on a PS4 Pro at a stable 30 FPS.
- **Screen mode setting for TVs that show a black screen.** EmuFive used the TV's preferred mode, which some TVs offer although the PS4 can't send it (black screen after the PS4 Multiboot menu). Add `emufive.mode=1920x1080@60` to the line in `/data/linux/boot/bootargs.txt` (keep `video=HDMI-A-1:1920x1080@60D` too).
- **A new emulator build** (KytyPS5 589bd14 with EmuFive patches 0001–0034).

### Update
Settings, System, Software update. The PS4 asks to restart after it.

From 1.0.3 or earlier, start the update once by hand (see the README's Changelog).

### New installs

releases.name: v1.0.9
releases.body:
## EmuFive 1.0.9: faster 3D games, video clips, game info

### What's new
- **3D games run much faster.** New GPU-shared game memory puts game memory where the PS4's GPU reads and writes it in place, so buffers are no longer copied, tracked page by page, or read back. Teardown on a PS4 Pro: the menu scene went from 2.1 to 7 FPS, and in game it runs at 9–12 FPS (about 20 in light scenes). It is on by default; if a game hangs or runs out of memory, turn it off in Settings > Games > GPU-shared game memory.
- **Fixes:** Teardown's crash in the main menu (it writes GPU commands from shaders), two crashes in long sessions, and a hang in Invincible VS.
- **Video clips.** PS + Triangle starts recording, in a game too, and PS + Triangle again stops it (720p or 1080p at 30 FPS, with sound, up to 60 minutes). Clips are saved on the PS4 (`~/Videos`) or in `PS5-videos` on a USB drive (Settings > Storage). Media shows and plays them, and Share sends them to your phone like screenshots. The PS4's video encoder can't be used under Linux, so the CPU encodes: about one core for 720p.

releases.name: v1.0.8
releases.body:
## EmuFive 1.0.8: big games run much faster

### What's new
- **Games with very large buffers run much faster.** 1.0.7 uploaded every recently used buffer whole each frame, which for a game like Teardown meant over 3 GB per frame. Now only small buffers (up to 4 MB) are uploaded that way; large ones are tracked by page again. Teardown on a PS4 Pro went from under 1 FPS to about 2.4 FPS. DREDGE keeps its 1.0.7 speed and clean sound.
- **A new emulator build** (KytyPS5 589bd14 with EmuFive patches 0001–0032).

### Teardown and other big games: more GPU memory
Teardown also needs the GPU to be allowed up to 5 GB of system RAM, or it stops with GPU out of memory. Use the `bootargs.txt` of [PS4 Multiboot v1.5.0-beta-5](https://github.com/blue0x1/ps4-multiboot/releases/tag/v1.5.0-beta.5) (copy it to `/data/linux/boot/` over FTP), or add `amdgpu.gttsize=5120 ttm.pages_limit=1310720` to the end of the line in your own.

### Update
Settings, System, Software update. No restart is needed. Coming from 1.0.6 or earlier, it installs 1.0.7 first, which also updates the PS4 Mesa (see the 1.0.7 notes).

From 1.0.3 or earlier, start the update once by hand (see the README's Changelog).

releases.body:
# 0.60.1 is out

There was a bug in the AppImage Updater Code. To fix this i have to revert to the old AppImage build and wait several weeks to ensure a smooth update process.

# 0.60.0 is out 🎉

This release is special for me. I build emuze with web technologies because that’s where I have the most experience, and I’m really proud of what I’ve achieved over the years. I’ve always wanted to help out in this wonderful emulation community, but aside from testing, I couldn’t do much to help with the emulators I love because I struggled with C++ code, which most emulators are written in. But sometimes you feel forced to try and try again. Since v0.59.0, I’ve successfully added a [change to RMG](https://github.com/Rosalie241/RMG/pull/518) to use the SDL GUID to identify a gamepad more reliably, and I forked Mednafen with [mednafen-sdl3](https://github.com/bmsuseluda/mednafen-sdl3) to greatly expand gamepad support. Those changes are just baby steps in the grand scheme of things, but they felt great, and I hope I can build on them in the future.

# 0.59.2 is out 🎉

This release is mostly preparation work to greatly reduce the file size of the AppImage with release 0.60.0.
Besides this fuse2 is not necessary anymore and Metainfos for AppImage Managers e.g. AM are included.

Please let me know what you think of it in the [emuze discord](https://discord.gg/tCzK7kc6Y4).

## 💥 Features
- added AppImage Metainfos
- AppImage works without fuse2
- Preparation work to greatly reduce the file size of the AppImage with release 0.60.0

# 0.59.0 is out 🎉

As you might now i love the simplicity of console gaming. You start the game and it just works. With emulation more often then not you have to provide more then just the game. You need things like a BIOS file, firmware or key files. I wanted to assist with this for a long time. With this release you can choose a folder where you can put your BIOS files and emuze will pick them up and configure the Emulators. Of course emuze will tell you if a required file is missing. On top of this emuze comes bundled with open source BIOS implementations for PlayStation, Game Boy Advance and NEO GEO. Of course you can use official BIOS files instead if you need by putting them in the BIOS folder. Sadly i was not able to achieve the same result for more complicated systems like PlayStation 3, WiiU and Switch. These systems require a installation of a firmware. I will try to tackle these in a future release.

Besides this i bundled and pre configured ScummVM and DOSBox Pure Unleashed.
Therefore the day is finally here: All 35 supported systems are pre configured and bundled now 🥳

# 0.58.0 is out 🎉

As one of the few nerdy kids in a small sleepy town in a country where arcade gaming was classified as gambling i could see lightgun games in magazines only. I had an NES and Captain N with his Zapper was sooo awesome to me. But when the time came that i could buy one with my own money the rise of flat panels began and with it the death of CRT TVs and Lightguns altogether. It was just a thing of the past, sadly.
But surprisingly the genre came back with the Wii and PS3 and there Pointer devices. Some years later camera based Lightguns came to the market and finally Lightgun gaming with the same and even higher precision is possible on flat panels.

## 💙 Thank you!

CosmoU 0.14.0 is full of ideas and bug reports from the CosmoU Discord – most of all from **Eduard** **. Thank you to everyone who tested the betas and wrote down every little thing. This update is yours! 🎉

## ✨ What's new

### 🎮 Switch 2 – a console of its own
- **Switch 2 support** – Settings → Games & Consoles → Add a console → **Switch 2**: choose your games folder and your Switch 2 emulator (**Eden-NX2**, **Eglantine** or one of their forks). Game files (`.xci`, `.nsp`) and dumped games (a folder with `exefs/main` inside) are found, updates and DLC are not counted as games.
- **✨ Its own interface** – with the Switch 2 on screen, CosmoU becomes a Switch 2: dark glass, the chosen game's colours behind everything, its title big above a row of large squares, one frame that glows in blue and red, a dock of round buttons. **Y** opens the **Library** (Recent · Most played · A–Z · Favorites, **/** searches), **+** a full **page for each game**, **Home** (or **Q**) **Quick Settings**. *Dark* and *Light*, soft sounds that play a little scale along the row.

releases.name: CosmoU 0.13.3
releases.body:
## 💙 Thank you, Eduard!

CosmoU 0.13.3 is built on ideas and bug reports by **Eduard** in the CosmoU Discord – pictures and music per console, your own order, marks, your own consoles, apps in full screen and so much more. Thank you for testing every beta and for every idea. This update is yours! 🎉

## ✨ What's new
### 🎨 One CosmoU, and a Switch that feels like a Switch
- **🎮 The Switch has its own interface** – with the Switch on screen, CosmoU looks and works like a Switch: **Home** with your last played games in one row (A starts the first one right away), round buttons below (All Software, Play Activity, Themes, Controllers, Consoles, System Settings, Power), **All Software** with sorting (**Y**) and search (**/**), a page for each game (**+**), **Quick Settings** on the Home button (or **Q**), *Basic White* and *Basic Black*, its own clicks. No Wii U Home, no Plaza, no buddies there. With a Wii U as well: the circles at the top left (or **L / R**) switch the whole window. Settings → Appearance → Switch → *Its own interface* turns it off.

releases.name: CosmoU 0.13.1
releases.body:
## 💙 Thank you, Eduard!

Everything in CosmoU 0.13.1 comes from ideas and bug reports by **Eduard** in the CosmoU Discord. Thank you for testing so much and for all the great ideas – this update is yours! 🎉

## ✨ What's new

### 🏝️ Your own picture and music for each console
**Settings → Appearance** has two new rows: **Background picture for …** and **Music for …**.
- Switch to a console (Wii U, Switch, 3DS …), choose any picture and any music file from your computer or phone – done.
- Every console keeps its own: your Zelda picture on the Wii U, something else on the Switch, another one on the 3DS.
- The picture lies behind the glass with a soft veil, so everything stays readable – it looks best with **Liquid Glass**.
- **Remove** brings back the theme's look and music.

### 🎨 Theme files with a picture
A `.cosmoutheme` can now bring a background picture, built on Liquid Glass:
```json
{ "name": "Great Sea", "base": "liquid-glass", "image": "sea.jpg", "music": "song.ogg" }
```
**Share** saves the theme with its picture and music. The guide: [docs/THEMES.md](https://github.com/Eryski/CosmoU/blob/main/docs/THEMES.md).

### ⏭️ Faster pages on the 3DS and Wii home screens

releases.name: CosmoU 0.13.0
releases.body:
## ✨ A calmer, clearer CosmoU

CosmoU 0.13 reworks the whole interface. All the features are still there, just sorted better, so every window and every theme feels like one product: easy to understand on the first start, calm with a big library, readable from the sofa.

## What changed

- **Play is always the strongest button** – in Covers, Grid, the Wii U Look and the game details. Details and the other actions are quieter.
- **Grid** – a calm banner: the cover sharp in front of its own softly blurred colours, instead of a giant pixelated picture.
- **Game details** – a smaller cover, Play first, *Add to favorites* as a quiet toggle, one line instead of four empty statistics before the first play, the tools in one row, save data and updates as simple rows.
- **Settings** – a calmer category bar (only the open category is in colour), a bigger search with its shortcut (Ctrl F / ⌘F).
- **Quick Menu** – your games first, then three clear groups: **Look**, **Sound** and **System**.
- **Theme gallery** – big cards with a preview picture of every theme.
- **Empty screens lead somewhere** – *Clear search*, *Show the library*, or the folder button of the console you're looking at.

releases.name: CosmoU 0.12.1
releases.body:
## A huge thanks to Eduard ❤️

Every fix and idea in this update came from **Eduard**, who tested CosmoU 0.12 in depth and reported everything on Discord. Thank you so much!

## New

- **Choose your console on start** – with more than one console, CosmoU starts with big console cards. D-pad to choose, A to pick, B to close. The console button at the top opens them too. You can turn this off in Settings → Look.
- **Right stick (R3) opens the game menu** – same as a right click, so adding favorites is quicker.

## Fixed

- **The portable Windows version is really portable now** – it keeps everything (settings, covers, music, themes, backups and a Cemu that CosmoU downloads) in a **CosmoU-data** folder next to the .exe instead of %APPDATA%. Your old settings are copied over on the first start.
- **Switch Home stopped at the 12th game** – the controller now reaches **All games** after the twelve most recent games: A shows every game, B goes back.
- **DS and 3DS covers were cut off on the left** – the top screen now shows the whole box.
- **Moving with the controller flashed like a page reload** on the console home screens – now only the selection moves.

emulators.latest_body:
GameNative for Mali handhelds, rebased on upstream GameNative 1.2.1.

**Proof of concept, released as is. No support:** I do not answer bug reports or questions, and I do not take requests for devices I do not own.

Download `gamenative-mali-modern.apk` below and install it. It installs next to the stock GameNative app (package `app.gamenative.mali`). It is debug-signed with this repository's fixed key, so it upgrades over earlier `mali` builds signed with the same key.

## What changed

- **Custom driver support for PanVK on Mali.** Import a Mesa PanVK package for your device in **Driver Manager**, then select it for a game under **Graphics**. No PanVK build is bundled, and the default stays the system driver.
- A Mali device no longer lists Turnip or Qualcomm drivers, and a container that names one falls back to the system driver.
- Rebased on upstream GameNative 1.2.1.

PanVK packages for the devices I own:
[Retroid Pocket 4 Pro](https://github.com/faux123/panvk-faux123-driver-rp4pro),
[Anbernic RG556](https://github.com/faux123/panvk-faux123-driver-rg556),
[GameForce Ace](https://github.com/faux123/panvk-faux123-driver-ace).

## Tested on

releases.name: FEX Release FEX-2611
releases.body:
# Read the blog post at [FEX-Emu's Site!](https://fex-emu.com/FEX-2611/)
You know the drill, it's been around a month so that means we have a new release landing. A smattering of changes all over the codebase this time.
Let's see what's interesting!

## CPU core index through TPIDRRO_EL0
This is a fun feature that has come about primarily because Windows on ARM mandates this feature. The [TPIDRRO_EL0](https://support.arm.com/documentation/ddi0601/2026-09/AArch64-Registers/TPIDRRO-EL0--EL0-Read-Only-Software-Thread-ID-Register?lang=en) register
is an ARM system register that is readable by userspace that the kernel can set to whatever 64-bit value it wants. In particular under Windows it is
part of their [ABI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/arm64-windows-abi-conventions?view=msvc-170#system-registers) that this register must
contain the current CPU core index once read. This gives ARM64/ARM64ec applications a really quick way to read what core it is executing on. This is
kind of a funny thing that needs to exist because **technically** the MPIDR_EL1 register is supposed to accomplish the same task. Although this

releases.name: FEX Release FEX-2610
releases.body:
# Read the blog post at [FEX-Emu's Site!](https://fex-emu.com/FEX-2610/)
We were a bit distracted this month with the [X.Org Developer's Conference](https://indico.freedesktop.org/event/12/) happening but we still managed
to get some work done. Let's jump in and see what has changed.

## JIT changes
This month brought some improvements to the JIT although less than typical. We added support for AVX-VNNI which is starting to get used by some game
libraries. We also optimized the SSE4.2 string operations so these are quite a bit faster. 3DNow! has been enabled again since we fixed the last known
bug with it. We also improved emulation on the x87 FXAM instruction since apparently Mono uses it to detect denormals for some reason. Additionally a
peephole optimization to improve a common case of an unmasked AVX gather instruction which some sound libraries rely on.

We also now have a software fallback for RDRAND and RDSEED instructions. This isn't enabled by default as the performance isn't as good as a hardware
implementation but it's useful for programs that mandate these instructions to exist. Also useful for platforms with Qualcomm Oryon where their RNG

releases.name: FEX Release FEX-2609
releases.body:
# Read the blog post at [FEX-Emu's Site!](https://fex-emu.com/FEX-2609/)
**"Kept you waiting, huh?"** - Solid Snake, professional sneaky man.

We're not going to sugar coat it, this last month was very busy and time just kept moving faster than expected.
A ton of work landed this month so we're going to just need to pick some of the highlights. Let's hop in!

# Jit work you say?
A bunch of random bug fixes and performance improvements landed this month. Primary things here are that there were various behaviour fixes for some
instructions. Undefined and defined flag fixes that FEX was messing up, some deadlock fixes, handling more cases that were previously asserts. There
was an optimization for the PMULHRSW instruction family that increased some Geekbench benchmark numbers. Surely some game uses it somewhere to notice
the 2x perf uplift. We also made the "full" self-modifying-code detection faster, which is used for Unity games in some instances. So that's nice.
We also reduced some lock-contention in the JIT so multiple threads jitting code at the same time should block each other less frequently.

There's more of course but come on we gotta go!

# Removed hacky unixlib fallbacks

releases.name: FEX Release FEX-2608
releases.body:
# Read the blog post at [FEX-Emu's Site!](https://fex-emu.com/FEX-2608/)
After what felt like a very quick month, it's time for another FEX release. We're busy writing improvements for next month's release already, so let's
not distract for too long and smash through these changes!

## Removal of deprecated FEXInterpreter binary
Back in the [FEX-2510](/FEX-2510) release we completely removed a **FEXLoader** binary with a deprecation of the **FEXInterpreter** binary, renaming it to
just **FEX**. We kept the FEXInterpreter binary around for a while because downstream projects had hardcoded the binary in their scripts and we wanted to give
some time for them to migrate. After nearly a year we're hoping that everyone has migrated to the new binary name. If your project is still using the
old binary name then we recommend fix them!

## The typical JIT improvements
As typical there are a bunch of JIT changes this month. Let's breakdown  what was fixed.

- Use SVE XAR for SHA1 emulation as a minor optimization.
- Fix JIT telemetry value unconstrained predictable problem on ARMv8.0
  - Would only cause some missed telemetry on ARMv8.0 platforms, very minor.

First Release

Features:
- Encrypt and decrypt 3ds roms (Supports batch).
- Patch roms with famous format (.ips, .ups, .bps, .ppf, .aps, .ebp, .dps, .xdelta)
- Hash files

## What's Changed
* DCNet: a free dedicated VPN service for Dreamcast games that only needs a basic Internet connection. 30 game servers are already available and more are coming.

# VKRT NES Remaster v0.1.0-rc.1

**First public preview — Windows x64 and experimental Linux x86-64**

VKRT NES Remaster is an open-source, native C++20 Nintendo Entertainment System emulator developed by Francisco Triemstra (VKRT).

It features a first-party NES emulation core with CPU, PPU, APU, cartridge and mapper implementations, alongside an observation-driven visual remastering system.

The remastering pipeline is designed to enhance presentation without changing the canonical emulation state.

## Games Supported: Metroid, Super Mario Bros. 3, Ninja Gaiden 3.

## Downloads

### Windows x64 — Tested Preview

- Native Windows desktop application.
- Original (F1) and Remaster (F4) presentation modes.
- Keyboard and controller support.
- Audio, fullscreen, ROM loading and save-state functionality.
- Built with MSVC 19.44.
- **41/41 automated tests passed, 0 failures.**
- Functional testing confirmed by the project owner.

**Installation:** Download the Windows ZIP, extract it and launch `VKRT NES Remaster.exe`.

### Linux x86-64 — Experimental

- Native C++20 Linux executable using X11/XWayland.
- Original (F1) and Remaster (F4) presentation modes.

  the game now draws the world with the screen's own aspect instead of stretching the 16:9 image: cars, wheels and
  buildings keep their shape and you see more of the world at the sides.

    to the whole screen, as before.

releases.name: Game Format Converter 2.1.0
releases.body:
**Game Format Converter 2.1.0** (formerly CHD Manager) adds a lot of formats. Everything new is described honestly in the README, including what was and wasn't tested.

## What's new

- **A new name.** CHD Manager is now Game Format Converter, because it converts far more than CHDs. It lives at a new repository address with new file names. **If you have an older CHD Manager, download this release once by hand: the old program can't find it by itself.** Your settings and keys don't carry over; put them in again under Settings for the optional features that use them.
- **Xbox 360:** ZAR (for Xenia), ISO and game folders. Hex-named download packages (Xbox Live Arcade, Games on Demand) aren't discs, so they are refused with an explanation.
- **Original Xbox:** a full dump becomes a trimmed `.xiso.iso` (7.8 GB down to just the game); also game folders and CHD.
- **PlayStation 3:** game folder to ISO and back, split pieces joined, `.pkg` packages unpacked and packed (with your own RPCS3 or your own key).
- **Nintendo Switch:** NSP to XCI and back, bundles with the newest update and DLC, one NSP per title, swapping in a newer update. **Switch 2:** folder to NUP and back (experimental).

releases.name: CHD Manager 2.0.1
releases.body:
> **CHD Manager is now Game Format Converter.** This is an old release. The current version is [Game Format Converter 2.1.0](https://github.com/Mr-Shizzy/Game-Format-Converter/releases/latest). The old program can't update itself to it, so please download it once by hand.

---

CHD Manager 2.0.1 is a small follow-up to 2.0.0 with two convenience fixes.

## What's fixed

- **Downloading the base PBP now selects it.** In Settings, after you press Download for the PSP base PBP, it is filled in and saved for you; no more browsing for it.
- **Moving the program folder no longer breaks saved paths.** If you move or rename the folder, the program notices at startup and points the saved paths (base PBP, chdman, Dolphin, artwork and output folders that were inside the old folder) at the new location.

## SHA-256

`CHD-Manager-2.0.1-win64.zip`: 4808e3e06adcfc41768b4c68b663afdc6aec0c213ed53f3dc3345b40ea656b3c

Unzip anywhere and run `CHD Manager.exe`. Python is not needed, and your settings carry over. The exe is **not code-signed**, so Windows SmartScreen may warn about an unknown publisher (More info, Run anyway). Full details and the list of what was and wasn't tested are in the README.

releases.name: CHD Manager 2.0.0
releases.body:
> **CHD Manager is now Game Format Converter.** This is an old release. The current version is [Game Format Converter 2.1.0](https://github.com/Mr-Shizzy/Game-Format-Converter/releases/latest). The old program can't update itself to it, so please download it once by hand.

---

CHD Manager 2.0.0 now converts PSP, GameCube, Wii and Wii U disc formats as well as CHD, PBP and CDI, checks that a conversion will fit on the drive before it starts, and is now free software under the GPL.

## What's new

- **New formats.** CSO and ZSO (PSP/PS2), ECM, and the GameCube/Wii family: ISO, RVZ, WIA, WBFS, GCZ and CISO, plus Wii U WUX/WUD in both directions. Archives (zip, tar, gz, 7z, rar) can be added directly.
- **Mode 1 error correction** for CD images, so a CUE/BIN with blank error-correction data becomes a complete, correct image.
- **Disk-space check.** Before each conversion the app estimates the space it will need (temporary files included) and refuses a job that clearly won't fit, with a plain message, instead of failing halfway.

releases.name: CHD Manager 1.4.0
releases.body:
> **CHD Manager is now Game Format Converter.** This is an old release. The current version is [Game Format Converter 2.1.0](https://github.com/Mr-Shizzy/Game-Format-Converter/releases/latest). The old program can't update itself to it, so please download it once by hand.

---

**You choose what happens to CHD files, and extraction now sorts out multi-file discs for you**

- **CHD files choice.** When a CHD is in the list, a **CHD files** choice appears at the top: **Extract** it, **Verify** it, or **Recompress** it with different compression (your original is kept). Right-click a file to give just that one a different action. The Action column always says what will happen.
- **Automatic one-BIN-per-track.** When extracting a CD, the app reads its track count first. A disc with several tracks (audio plus data) gets one BIN per track; a one-track disc gets a single BIN. No setting to remember. You can still force "one BIN per track" or "one single BIN".
- **Tidy batches.** Anything that comes out as several files (split CDs, Dreamcast GDI) is put in its own folder named after the disc, so a big batch doesn't turn into a pile of mixed-up files.

releases.name: CHD Manager 1.3.0
releases.body:

---

**A calmer, simpler main window**

- One list of discs, one line saying which settings will be used, and one Start button. That's the whole main screen.
- The five tabs moved into a **Settings window** (the **More** menu, or **Change settings...**). It has the conversion options, output folder, the suggested-settings explanation, and an About page.
- The log is hidden until you click **Show log**. It opens by itself if something fails.
- Less common actions (info, verify selected, light/dark theme) are in the **More** menu.
- The table no longer shows the Folder column. The header is slimmer and spacing is roomier.
- The version buttons at the bottom of the window (`chdman 0.289` and `CHD Manager 1.3.0`) are now the update buttons: click one to check for an update, and it turns orange when one is waiting.
- Nothing about how discs are converted, extracted or verified changed.

emulators.description: Sega 系模拟器，覆盖 Genesis、Game Gear、32X 与 Sega CD。

releases.name: GenX v1.1.4
releases.body:
Fixes for the games reported on GitHub, PlayStation controllers, and the
Master System's Light Phaser and paddle.

**Download:** `GenX-v1.1.4-win64.zip`. Unzip it anywhere and run `genx.exe`.
To update, replace your old `genx.exe` with the new one. Your settings and
saves stay where they are.

### New

- **PlayStation controllers.** A DualShock 4 or DualSense is recognised and
  laid out like an Xbox pad, with its own button names in the Input tab. A
  DualShock 3 works through DsHidMini.
- **Automatic controller choice.** GenX uses whatever pad is plugged in, and
  the keyboard when there's none. New installs start on it; pick it in
  **Configure → Input** if you already have settings.
- **Master System Light Phaser and Paddle Control**, aimed with the mouse,
  plugged in by themselves for the games that need them.
- **Light gun games get their gun by themselves**, on the Mega Drive and the
  Sega CD.

### Fixed

- **Pier Solar** now plays and saves.
- **Back to the Future Part III (Europe)** starts on the Master System and
  the Mega Drive. Other European games that need a 50Hz console get one.
- **50Hz games no longer run 20% fast**, including Fantastic Dizzy.

releases.name: GenX v1.1.3
releases.body:
Play your real Sega CD discs. Nothing else in the emulation changed.

**Download:** `GenX-v1.1.3-win64.zip`. Unzip it anywhere and run `genx.exe`.
To update, replace your old `genx.exe` with the new one. Your settings and
saves stay where they are.

### New

- **Sega CD discs straight from your PC's CD/DVD drive.** Put the disc in,
  choose **File → Open ROM → Sega CD from drive**, and pick the drive. GenX
  reads the game and its CD music from the disc, reading ahead while you play
  so the drive keeps up. A USB drive works too.
- **Changing discs:** use **Sega CD → Swap to disc in drive**, or just put the
  next disc in the drive. GenX swaps it in as a real Sega CD would.
- **Front ends:** `genx.exe E:\` starts the disc in drive E:.

You still need the Sega CD BIOS for the disc's region.

If your drive or a disc doesn't work, please
[open an issue](https://github.com/GamesExObscura/GenX/issues) with the drive's
make and model and the game.

See the [changelog](https://github.com/GamesExObscura/GenX/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
for every change.

Windows may show a SmartScreen warning because the exe isn't code-signed.
Choose **More info → Run anyway**.

releases.name: GenX v1.1.2
releases.body:
Sega CD fixes. Nothing else in the emulation changed.

**Download:** `GenX-v1.1.2-win64.zip`. Unzip it anywhere and run `genx.exe`.
To update, replace your old `genx.exe` with the new one. Your settings and
saves stay where they are.

### Fixed

- **Crash when opening a Sega CD disc.** GenX closed without a message when a
  disc sat near a file or folder whose name has certain characters, such as an
  accent stored as a separate mark (some "Pokémon" names) or Japanese text.
- **Japanese and Southeast Asian Sega CD BIOSes now start.** They used to stop
  on an error such as "This is a PAL-compatible Mega CD for exclusive use in
  Southeast Asia", because GenX always presented itself as a US or European
  console. GenX now becomes the console the BIOS belongs to.
- **Japanese discs get a Japanese BIOS** when your BIOS folder also holds the
  Southeast Asian one. Some BIOS packs name the Southeast Asian BIOS
  `jp_mcd1_9112.bin`, which GenX used to pick first.
- The **BIOS** tab in **Configure** shows the BIOS each region's discs will
  really use.

Thanks to the player who reported the Southeast Asia error.

releases.name: GenX v1.1.1

emulators.description: PlayStation 5 的 Android 模拟器，基于 KytyPS5 与 FEX。
emulators.latest_body:
Sixth alpha of the first PlayStation 5 emulator for Android, and the first with **PS4 backward compatibility**: PS4 games now run in CapyPS5 the way they do on a real PS5. Existing installs are offered this update in the app.

**New: PS4 backward compatibility**

A PS5 runs PS4 games on its own hardware. CapyPS5 does the same in software: PS4 games use the same x86-64 JIT, system libraries and Vulkan renderer as PS5 games, and only what the PS4 does differently was added.
- **GPU:** PS4 (GCN gfx7) shaders and registers, PS4 render targets and texture tiling, CMASK and HTile fast clears, cube and volume textures, and the PS4 Gnm driver calls.
- **System:** PS4 executables and the modules games ship, the PS4 memory layout and flexible memory budget, and PS4 save data and trophies.
- PS4 games go in the same game folders as PS5 games (a folder with `eboot.bin` and `sce_sys/param.sfo`) and carry a **PS4** mark in the library.
- This is the first release with it. 2D and Unity games run best; Unreal Engine 4 games start but are slow; many games don't boot yet. Lower the resolution for big games.

**Also new**

- This is the first release with it. 2D and Unity games run best; Unreal Engine 4 games start but are slow; many games don't boot yet. Lower the resolution for big games.

**Also new**

releases.name: CapyPS5 v0.0.5
releases.body:
Fifth alpha of the first PlayStation 5 emulator for Android. Mali GPUs on their system driver can now run games, and the FPS counter shows how many frames CapyPS5 Framegen adds. Existing installs are offered this update in the app.

**New**
- **Mali on the system driver:** that driver cannot sample BCn compressed textures, so the GPU used to be rejected. CapyPS5 now decompresses those textures on the GPU when it uploads them (BC1 to BC7, including BC6H HDR textures). GPUs that support BCn keep using it directly.
- **PanVK on Mali:** the GPU is no longer rejected when the driver lacks vertex-stage stores or dual-source blending.
- **Framegen counter:** with CapyPS5 Framegen on, the FPS counter reads *XX FPS - YY FG*: XX are the game's own frames, YY the total including generated ones. The options are now called *Framegen x2*, *x3* and *x4*.
- **HDR10 output:** games that output HDR10 are converted to SDR for the screen.

**Fixed**
- Tessellation: quad domains, fractional-even spacing, counterclockwise output and masked hull control points.

releases.name: CapyPS5 v0.0.4
releases.body:
Fourth alpha of the first PlayStation 5 emulator for Android. More than 100 games now run correctly according to testers' reports, and this release adds CapyPS5 Framegen. Existing installs are offered this update in the app.

**New**
- **CapyPS5 Framegen:** optional frame generation. It draws in-between frames from the motion between two game frames, so a game at 30 FPS is shown at 60. Off by default; turn it on in *Settings → Performance* (1 per frame, or up to 3). Adds one frame of latency and some GPU load; works best from 25 FPS up.
- New performance options in *Settings → Performance*: shadow resolution, early depth testing and a frame rate limit (30 or 20 FPS).
- Physical keyboard input and an on-screen keyboard toggle for text fields, and system dialogs that can now be answered.
- Android 16 and devices with 16 KB memory pages are supported.

**Fixed**
- Unreal Engine 5 games: graphics and async compute hand work back and forth several times per frame, and each hand-off waited up to 100 ms. Menus that ran at 0–2 FPS now move.
- Games whose shadows use depth-compare texture gathers (Castlevania: Belmont's Curse) closed after the menu.

releases.name: CapyPS5 v0.0.3
releases.body:
Third alpha of the first PlayStation 5 emulator for Android. Fixes for the logs testers sent on v0.0.2, CPU work for Unreal Engine games, and more from KytyPS5. Existing installs are offered this update in the app.

**Fixed**
- Games that use fibers (sceFiber) closed the emulator at start on ARM ("Fiber context switching is only implemented on x86_64", Toy Story Retro Roundup). Fibers now switch the game's own registers. First support: please report how fiber games behave.
- Final Fantasy VII Rebirth: sceKernelFtruncate, which it calls when saving, is now available.
- Mewgenics: pthread_setcanceltype is now available.
- The game clock (RDTSC) ran about 23 % faster than the frequency games are told; they now match.
- Very large GPU compute dispatches (over 65535 groups, as in Astro Bot) are split to fit Adreno limits.
- Unity backtraces no longer follow a bogus frame at the start of each guest thread.

**New**
- Unreal Engine games: the TLS and process clock reads they make millions of times a second run inside the game code instead of calling into the emulator.
- Shaders can read the real GPU clock (S_MEMREALTIME) on drivers that offer it.

releases.name: CapyPS5 v0.0.2 (Alpha)
releases.body:
Second alpha of the first PlayStation 5 emulator for Android. Fixes for what testers reported on v0.0.1, a trophy screen, and 60 games on the compatibility list. Existing installs are offered this update in the app.

**Fixed**
- Virtual controller: several buttons can now be held at once.
- Physical controllers: the left stick no longer presses the d-pad (it moved menus and cursors, as in Mewgenics).
- Adreno 6xx with Turnip (such as Adreno 660) no longer closes at start for lack of 8-bit storage (thanks to deivid22srk).
- Dead Cells has its music, hits and footsteps back: NGS2 voices sent to a rack handle are now heard.
- Games that use user clip planes or uncommon storage texture settings no longer close.

**New**
- Trophies: each game's trophy list, what you have earned, and a card to share your progress.
- A "What's new" card after each update.
- Over 35 improvements from KytyPS5: shaders, tessellation, NGS2 and ATRAC9 audio, flip waits and fewer crashes.

releases.body:
## Lemon-Project v1.5.0

One Lemon for everyone: three modes replace the separate builds, the GPU is emulated on its own thread by default, and a round of fixes from your logs. Welcome to **rcssf**, the newest member of Team Lemon.

### New
- **Speed, Normal and Quality modes**, the first card in Settings. One choice sets resolution, filtering, anti-aliasing, GPU mode and shader building. Speed: 0.75x, bilinear, Fast GPU mode, asynchronous shaders. Normal (the default): 1x, Accurate GPU mode. Quality: 2x, bicubic, FXAA, Accurate. Change any of those afterwards and the card shows Custom. Modes are also in the in-game menu, in a game's menu in the library (for that game only) and in the quick settings tile.
- **Lemon Lite becomes the Speed mode.** This is the last Lemon Lite: it tells you, keeps its lighter settings as the Speed mode and takes you to Lemon. Install Lemon and use "Migrate from another emulator" in its Settings to bring your saves, keys and firmware over.
- **Lemon Lite & Spoofed becomes Lemon Spoofed**: plain Lemon under a benchmark app's package name, with no settings of its own. Lite & Spoofed installs update into it with their data.

releases.name: Lemon-Project v1.4.1
releases.body:
## Lemon-Project v1.4.1

**If you installed 1.4.0:** it closed as soon as it opened, in all three variants, and it has been withdrawn. Sorry about that! Download this version from this page, because the app can't update itself when it doesn't open. Install it over 1.4.0 and your data stays as it was.

Thanks once more to **BitRanger** for 21 pull requests (GitHub #25 to #45). This is what's new since 1.3.0:

### New
- **Several quick saves.** Each Quick Save goes into a new slot and Quick Load loads the newest, so a badly timed save no longer replaces the only one. "Quick saves to keep" goes from 1 to 4 (2 by default; each takes 1 to 2 GB). **Load save**, in the in-game menu and as a hotkey, lists this session's saves with a picture and how long ago each was made. Loading an older one asks first, because it deletes the newer ones. (BitRanger)
- **Toggle and turbo on on-screen buttons.** In the overlay editor, tap a button and choose how it behaves: Normal, Toggle (a tap holds it down, the next tap lets it go, and it looks pressed meanwhile) or Turbo (it repeats while your finger is on it). Saved with the layout, so each game can have its own.

releases.name: Lemon-Project v1.3.0
releases.body:
## Lemon-Project v1.3.0

Gamepad hotkeys, cheat downloads and a much steadier Quick Save/Load. Thanks again to **BitRanger** for seven more pull requests (GitHub #17 to #23), and welcome to Team Lemon!

### New
- **Gamepad hotkeys** (Settings → Controls → Hotkeys). Pick a Hotkey Enable button, then give each action the buttons to hold with it: Quick Save, Quick Load, show or hide the performance stats and the device info overlays, pause or unpause, and exit (it takes a second press unless "Confirm on Exit?" is turned off). # Lumen Emu 0.1.0 build 5 for iOS and iPadOS

This preview targets ARM64 iPhones and iPads running iOS or iPadOS 17.4 or later. The IPA is intended for sideloading and local signing with AltStore Classic. Both the PS4 and PS5 cores require JIT. Installing this build and enabling JIT through AltStore Classic still need to be verified on a physical iPhone.

## Testing and compatibility

**Lumen Emu 0.1.7, build 10** updates the GitHub APK with a quick folder browser, direct access to your existing game library, PS4 audio fixes and the latest cumulative core changes.

### Library and interface

- Choose your game folder quickly and use its files in place after granting Android’s all-files access. No private copy is required for the GitHub APK.

releases.name: Lumen Emu 0.1.6 — Faster loading, Banners & automatic PanVK
releases.body:
## Massive loading improvements and experimental Mali support

**Lumen Emu 0.1.6 brings a massive loading speedup in the tested PS5 startup path, restores direct local-ROM access for both PS4 and PS5, bundles Turnip Banners, and adds automatic experimental PanVK selection for compatible Mali GPUs.**

### Faster loading

- Local ROM folders now use direct filesystem reads after granting Android's all-files access, avoiding repeated document-provider work during loading.
- The system folder picker remains available. Recognised local filesystem folders use the direct path; other supported providers retain the document bridge.
- Document-backed libraries also benefit from reduced path lookups, provider acquisition and directory-enumeration overhead, plus improved native file-size queries.
- The single active library and optional verified folder moves are preserved.

releases.name: Winlator Mali Bionic 1.2.1
releases.body:
# Winlator Mali Bionic 1.2.1

A fixes-and-polish update to 1.2.

## ⚠️ Reinstall Required!
Uninstall the old version and install 1.2.1 fresh. Back up your game saves first (Save Manager, or copy them out of your container). Containers made on 1.2 are not carried over.

## Fixes for 1.2 user reports
- Fixed a reboot on some MediaTek Mali phones (JM Mali).
- Fixed a crash when opening a shortcut.
- Fixed the controller binding editor.
- Fixed the stutter when holding D-pad right.
- Fixed File Manager not opening (it needed `libcdio.dll`), and File Manager hanging on x86_64 Wine (replaced with Bannerlator's newer `wfm.exe` / `winhandler.exe`).

## Graphics and performance
- **Fullscreen modes:** Fit, Stretch, Fill and Integer, plus screen alignment (Center, Top, Bottom half), set per container or per game and changeable live in Display & Session.
- **EGL stripes fixed:** CPU writes into the window buffer are flushed per X batch.
- **ZeroFG:** the default multiplier is capped at the display refresh rate (40 fps on a 60 Hz screen now gives 1.5x instead of 2x with dropped frames).
- **Gladio:** refuses OpenGL contexts above 3.3 again; libGL stripped of debug info (1.48 MB to 488 KB).

releases.name: Winlator Mali Bionic 1.2
releases.body:
Winlator Mali Bionic v1.2 Winlator Mali Bionic v1.2 is a major architectural overhaul over v1.1, introducing a native EGL rendering engine, ZeroFG Vulkan compute frame interpolation, a redesigned UI with Madeira Liquid Glass touch controls, two selectable BCn layers, hardware performance tools, kernel-direct telemetry, and a cloud-powered community configuration ecosystem. ⚠️ Reinstall Required!
🖥️ Native EGL Rendering Engine & Gladio Integration
  • High-Performance Native EGL Architecture: Migrated from the legacy v1.1 rendering stack (GLRenderer, DisplayX, VirGL, blit_converter, and Java EffectComposer) to Pipetto-crypto's native C++ EGL renderer at app/src/main/cpp/winlator/renderer/egl.cpp.
  • Elimination of Legacy Overhead: Removed the legacy DisplayX layer (displayx.cpp, DisplayXView), VirGL (VirGLRendererComponent), and blit_converter.cpp, eliminating over 3,500 lines of redundant CPU blit and synchronization code.

releases.name: Winlator Mali Bionic 1.1
releases.body:
Winlator Mali Bionic v1.1

🚀 New Features

- Added Fake HDR.
- Added a Universal FPS Limiter.
- Added a Sharpness option.
- Added GTA V Optimization toggle in Shortcut Settings.
- Added DXVK Config toggle with built-in pre-made configuration presets.
- Automatically generates a dxvk.conf file for each container based on the selected preset.
- Added new DXVK versions.
- Added the new GameNative Vulkan Wrapper.
- Added new Box64 and FEX presets.

---

🎮 Unreal Engine 3 Preset

- Added a dedicated Unreal Engine 3 preset.
- Tested with X-Men Origins: Wolverine for improved compatibility and performance.

---

⚙️ Hybrid x86 FEXCore

- Added a custom Hybrid x86 FEXCore.

What does it do?

- Improves compatibility while maintaining high performance.
- Fixes physics issues in supported games that normally require x86 Reduced Precision to be completely disabled.

Why is it better?

Normally, disabling x86 Reduced Precision forces software emulation for all x86 code, which can significantly reduce performance.

Hybrid x86 only uses software emulation where it is actually needed (such as physics calculations), while allowing the rest of the game to run natively for much better performance.

releases.name: Winlator Mali Bionic 1.0 ( Updated Again )
releases.body:
Winlator Mali Bionic v1.0

New Features

- Multiple Vulkan Wrapper Selection — Select between Wrapper, Wrapper-Leegao, and Wrapper V2 on a per-container basis.
- ASTC Transcoding — Native ASTC texture transcoding using a modified version of leegao's bcn_layer with improved performance, memory usage, and stability.
- ETC2 Transcoding — Native ETC2 texture transcoding using a modified version of leegao's bcn_layer with improved performance, memory usage, and stability.
- Apex Frame Generation — Based on Motion Compute Frame Interpolator (MCFI), with additional implementation and optimizations for improved performance, stability, and compatibility. Apex also utilizes GPU resources alongside the game and may impact performance depending on your device.
- Advanced HUD — Enhanced in-game overlay based on Winlator Ludashi's HUD with additional refinements.
- Unified Control System — XInput, DInput, and Exclusive input modes have been unified into a single control system.
- Graphics Driver Manager — Install and manage Vulkan Wrappers and bcn_layer directly from local storage. User-installed drivers automatically take priority over bundled versions.

> **System Settings** → **Privacy & Security**, scroll down to **Security**, click
> **Open Anyway** and confirm.
>
> A package older than v1.1.2 says *"POM2 is damaged"* instead and has no
> **Open Anyway**. Do not move it to the Trash. Run this in Terminal:
>
> ```bash
> xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/POM2.app
> ```
>
> **🪟 Windows: "Windows protected your PC".** Click **More info**, then
> **Run anyway**.

- **Porte Parole:** speech synthesis now uses Sébastien Pourcel's MEA8000 engine.

**Fixed: "POM2 is damaged" on macOS.** An accented file name in the package
broke the app's signature when the Finder copied it into *Applications*. macOS
then called the app damaged and offered no way to allow it from System Settings.

The emulator itself is unchanged from
[v1.1.0](https://github.com/habib256/pom2/releases/tag/v1.1.0), which has the
full list of new features. v1.1.1 was tagged but never published.

releases.name: POM2 v1.1.0
releases.body:
**New hardware.** Eight cards — Microsoft SoftCard II, PCPI Applicard,
Premium SoftCard //e, ALS CP/M Card, Saturn 128K, Videx UltraTerm, DAN ][
Controller, E-Z Color (TMS9918A, with its own Card Monitor tab) — and an
OS-call trace (ProDOS MLI, SmartPort, Pascal BIOS, Monitor, CP/M BDOS, …).

**No copyrighted firmware ships.** A Disk II boots on POM2's own boot PROM
and data separator; a first launch offers to download the rest.

**Closer to the silicon.** All 801 comments that cite MAME or AppleWin were
re-read against the primary sources — datasheets, Sather, Apple's technical
notes, format specifications, ROM disassemblies — in 33 reports under
`docs/audits/`. Where POM2 and those sources disagreed, 3 major and 26 minor
fixes followed: a `SAVE` that disarmed the //c motor timer, a 6551 IRQ the
datasheet does not allow, a Z8530 write that stopped the transmitter, a FLUX
track losing one transition per revolution, a same-value 6522 store that
re-strobed the AY, five ImageWriter power-on defaults. Where POM2's reading
of a datasheet differs from another emulator's, the divergence is now
documented in the code rather than silently aligned. Every hardware claim

releases.name: POM2 v1.0.0

The first stable release: the Apple ][, ][+, //e, //c and //c Plus, in NTSC
and PAL, with the cards, media and tools listed in the README.

- **macOS:** relative paths and the first launch of a downloaded copy work.
- **Many fixes** from bug hunts against MAME, AppleWin and the data sheets.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/habib256/pom2/compare/v0.9.9...v1.0.0)

Hitode 0.2.8 expands iOS and Android launcher support and improves video, audio, text, and UI compatibility across games. / Hitode 0.2.8 完善了 iOS 与 Android 端体验，并全面提升了音视频、字体渲染与界面交互的兼容性。

## Changes / 更新内容

- **Launcher & Library:** Added manual library sorting, an option to remove managed game copies when deleting a game, Traditional Chinese (Big5) encoding selection, pause-menu fast-forward key mode, earlier exit during loading, and direct settings links on launch failures.
- **iOS:** Enabled built-in JIT inside LiveContainer, improved StikJIT / RemotePairing connection discovery, and declared the increased-memory-limit entitlement with installation guidance when missing.
- **Android:** Added direct access to writable external storage, streamlined storage permission and folder import prompts, adapted touch controls to side gesture strips, added a hide-controls mode, refined the soft-keyboard text bar (with Backspace), and fixed startup IPC failures.

- 游戏内的网页和邮件链接现在由系统默认应用打开；启动错误会指出缺失的 DLL。
- 改善了一些反人类的交互。

## Banana Native v0.3.45

- **Pokémon Pokopia:** native 4:3 UI and rendering for v2.0.1.

releases.name: Hokkaido 0.7.0
releases.body:
# Hokkaido 0.7.0

The biggest Hokkaido release so far: a second engine. Next to Hokkaido's emulator, the APK now carries [Banana Native](https://git.eden-emu.dev/moceure/BananaNative), which runs a Switch 2 game's code natively on the phone and draws its graphics through Vulkan. You choose the engine per game, and Banana Native runs behind Hokkaido's own screens, with Hokkaido's GPU driver, saves and settings.

Tested on a Samsung Galaxy S26 (Exynos 2600, Xclipse 960, 12 GB), a Galaxy S24 (Exynos 2400, Xclipse 940, 8 GB) and a Galaxy S25 (Snapdragon 8 Elite, Adreno 830, 12 GB), all on Android 17.

**Updating:** install the APK over 0.6.x. Your games, saves and settings stay. Every game keeps running on the Hokkaido engine unless Banana Native has a playable profile for it (see Auto below), and you can switch any game back in Game properties.

## Getting started with Banana Native

1. **GPU driver.** On an Xclipse GPU (Exynos), install a custom RADV driver in Hokkaido's GPU driver manager, globally or for the game. Banana Native uses the same driver as Hokkaido.

releases.name: Hokkaido 0.6.6
releases.body:
# Hokkaido 0.6.6

Tested on a Samsung Galaxy S26 (Exynos 2600, Xclipse 960, 12 GB) and a Galaxy S25 (Snapdragon 8 Elite, Adreno 830, 12 GB), both on Android 17. The performance work tested on the S26's Exynos carries over well to Snapdragon.

## New in 0.6.6

- **Pokopia's sky renders.** Under NCE, a game read from memory the GPU had drawn into was treated as a write, which threw the GPU's result away. Such reads now fetch the GPU's data, and reactive flushing is kept on for Pokopia. Both apply to Pokopia only. Thanks to Diriande for the fix (#17), our first outside contribution.
