releases.name: melonRA 0.5.1
releases.body:
# Changes (**Mainly bugfixes!**)
- Linux: Accepting a Netplay invite through Discord without having melonRA open would show an "Unknown protocol" error message, this was because it wasn't registered properly with the rest of apps in the OS, it now handles it properly.
- Netplay: Errors whilst syncing up instances and saves with the "hidden consoles" used for Netplay.
- Netplay: Closing the room closes the open UDP port after a while.
- Netplay: Closing a room with nobody connected is now instant.
- _Other minor Netplay fixes._
- Rewind kept its history after inserting a cartridge or booting up firmware. Meaning that, rewinding could make you rewind to a previous game. This has been patched.
- _Other general fixes._
- Casual mode offline unlocks were dropped if the saved login expired when its sent, now it is kept for the next login. And now the text is clearer when you play offline.

releases.name: melonRA 0.5.0
releases.body:
# Additions and changes
- There's a new and more concise **settings window** which shows all categories of settings in the same window without having to close and open them separately.
- **The name of the game is shown in the window title now, as well as its icon in the taskbar.**
- **"Hybrid Single"** as a new screen layout mode, literally the same as _Hybrid_, but without the mirroring of the top screen. _(Perfect for dyslexic people, like me! :D)_
- New **Time Played** and **Last Played** columns on the game list.
- **New option to mark games as "Favorite"** (it shows with a little heart besides the title, same place as the mastery and game settings cog) and a new tab for all favorite games.
- The ability to **make a desktop shortcut** for any game, which uses the actual icon of the ROM.
- **Thumbnails** for every save state slot.
- New option to **resume where you left off last session.** (Found in _Interface Settings_)
- New Rewind hotkey, must be enabled also in _Interface Settings_ alongside the amount of seconds you can rewind back to.
- **Trimmed the executable** so its a smaller download overall.

releases.name: melonRA 0.4.0
releases.body:
**NOTE:** As of today, 28/10, the emulator isn't yet verified for Hardcore completions in RetroAchievements' side. Some features might not be available just yet.

# Additions and changes
- **Discord Rich Presence** is now available, shows the emulator's name, the logo and header name of the ROM you are playing. When paired with RetroAchievements, shows details of their own Rich Presence on Discord (showing what you are doing in the game, the icon of the game's set, etc.)
- Some game list changes, including a new option **to display an achievement completion bar**, it'll turn gold when the game is Mastered. And it will show a little star in the title of the game, or in the cover when in grid mode.
- You can now right click games in the list and click "Achievements..." **it'll take you to that game's achievement page** where you can see your progress.
- A **hotkey to rotate the screens has been added** under Input and Hotkeys > General Hotkeys. Useful for games that require a lot of screen layout changes and rotation.

releases.name: melonRA 0.3.0
releases.body:
**NOTE:** As of today, 10/27, RetroAchievements hasn't yet verified the emulator for Hardcore support. So some features might not completely work as intended.

**NOTE 2:** Version no longer available because of updater changes for security reasons.

# Additions and changes
- **You can now unlock achievements whilst offline**, it will save the achievement data and will unlock them once it can reach the server again. (Both _Hardcore_ and _Casual_)
- Challenge indicators in the overlay are able to be **hovered on**, showing the requisites for the challenge itself and how many points its worth.
- **Quick screen layout and sizing hotkeys** (under _General Hotkeys_ in _Input and Hotkeys_ tab)
- **Game list has been optimised** so that it remembers your games already attributed, and only updates when it detects new ones or deletes when it doesn't see them in the directory.
- **Settings can now be exported and restored** from one system to another (excluding RetroAchievements login info)
- _Kaeru WFC_ and _Wiimmfii_ support in the **online play server picker** under _Wi-Fi Settings_

releases.name: melonRA 0.2.0
releases.body:
**NOTE:** Version no longer available because of updater changes for security reasons.

# Additions and changes
 - **Game list:** Now instead of the default melonDS starting screen, the emulator will prompt you to add a path for your games, and thus will put them in a modern, slicker game list that shows you the title of the game, its icon, region (and a flag!) and developer. 
 - The game list can be set to a **grid mode**, which will parse the covers of your downloaded library and make them appear uniformly in a square grid, you are able to change the sizing of this grid with a slider.
- **RetroAchievements sets** from your populated game list can all be viewed under "Achievements..." on the "RetroAchievements" tab. Your currently playing sits at the top showing all the subsets, whilst the rest are in a list to the side.
- **Overlay customisation:** you can now choose where elements are positioned in the screen under "Settings..." on the "RetroAchievements" tab. You will be able to choose where certain elements appear, and their visuals (such as having bolded text, making them smaller, or changing the colors to a simpler scheme)

Apologies for the rename of the repo but its easier to do now rather than later (I chose the old name poorly).

releases.name: Mesen 2.1.0
releases.body:
Requirements
-
For the **macOS** and **Linux** builds, **SDL2** must be manually installed first.

Changelog
-
A lot has been improved or added since the first release of 2.0.0 over 2 years ago.
This is a short summary of the most notable changes.

- Support for more consoles:
  - Game Boy Advance
  - Game Gear
  - Master System (including support for the SG-1000 and ColecoVision)
  - Wonder Swan and Wonder Swan Color
- Accuracy improvements for all consoles
- Various bug fixes
- macOS support
- New features and improvements for the debugger:
  - Forbid breakpoints
  - Step back single scanline/frame
  - Undo ROM/RAM changes
  - Integration with more compilers/assemblers (HuCC, PCEAS, SDCC, devkitARM)
- Console-specific improvements/fixes:
  - NES: Support for EPSM audio and the Rainbow mapper
  - SNES: Fixed freezes in Battle Grand Prix and Kishin Douji Zenki
  - SNES: Added support for ST018 (Hayazashi Nidan Morita Shogi 2)
  - PCE: Improved VRAM read/write timings - fixes issues in Wonder Momo.
  - PCE: Improved CD-ROM load timings - fixes issues in Brandish and Sherlock Holmes.
  - PCE: Fixed Arcade Card emulation bug - fixes invisible characters in Garou Densetsu Special

emulators.name: MetroidPrimePort
emulators.description: 《银河战士 Prime》的反编译移植，支持 Linux、Windows、Android。
emulators.latest_body:
**You need your own disc image:** Metroid Prime Trilogy (`R3ME01` USA, `R3MP01` PAL), Metroid Prime USA (`GM8E01`, revisions 1.00, 1.01 and 1.02), PAL (`GM8P01`). No disc image or game assets are included.

## What changed

### Metroid Prime Remastered graphics
- The arm cannon, suit arm and grapple arm use Remastered's own Thermal and X-Ray Visor models.
- The Chozo Ghosts, Oculus and other enemies use their Remastered X-Ray models.

releases.name: Moonlight Android v12.0
releases.body:

# 说明
此版本为热修复版本，你可以选择覆盖原有apk或者删除原apk重新安装。
# 更新内容
- Wine：加入Proton-Wine，你可以在附加内容中进行下载安装
- APK：优化输入法弹出方式，不再延迟500毫秒
# Bug修复
- MangoHud：优化骁龙GPU监控性能，修复Adreno卡顿和N/A跳变
- APK：修复默认变量在删除后被重复加入的问题
- APK：修复Box版本无法独立的问题
- APK：修复 dxvk 带版本号时的空指针崩溃
# 常见问题说明
- 由于Termux-X11的渲染问题，在容器中使用"创建快捷方式"功能的时候会触发渲染错误，退出容器后重新启动即可解决，此问题并不影响快捷方式的创建
- 由于a8xx架构处理器将路径锁死，用户态没有权限读取GPU的实时数据，所以a8xx设备在使用MangoHud和安卓层面的性能监控的时候GPU占用会显示N/A，大部分a7xx设备都可以正常读取GPU占用率，因为我没有a6xx所以无法获取测试数据
- 在使用虚拟控件的过程中如果发现视角被限制无法移动，请在触控设置中打开"相对光标移动"选项
emulators.note: 与 afeimod 的 glibc 版本是两个独立分支。

releases.name: Winlator-Glibc v2.0
releases.body:
# 说明
从Winlator-Glibc v2版本开始项目将使用全新命名空间，这意味着你可以无需删除曾经的v1或者7.1.6版本即可安装此版本，但是我依然推荐你将曾经的版本删除，以后我将只为拥有新命名空间的版本进行软件包的更新与维护，新旧版本的 Wine、Box64、Turnip 等组件不再兼容，也无法混用。
# 更新内容
- 使用全新安卓命名空间
- 重新编译rootfs
- 支持 Vulkan 1.4+ API
- 弃用X Server服务，使用Termux-X11作为显示后端（来自[ewt45](https://github.com/[ewt45](https://github.com/ewt45))）
- 升级Zink版本，Zink版本将与Turnip版本同步更新
- 添加Freedreno驱动支持
- 补全GStreamer环境，当前版本：稳定版 v1.28.3（来自[Waim908](https://github.com/Waim908)）
- 升级MangoHud版本，当前版本：正式版 v0.8.4
- 优化安卓层面的性能监控，GPU采用获取真实数据逻辑
- 添加KDE桌面鼠标主题，可在编辑容器界面中的Wine配置选项中切换主题与鼠标大小
# Bug修复
- 修复启动容器与退出容器有几率崩溃的问题（来自[ewt45](https://github.com/[ewt45](https://github.com/ewt45))）
- 修复摇杆无法自由移动的问题
- 修复快捷方式中"添加到主屏幕"功能不可用的问题
- 修复虚拟控件手柄摇杆有几率卡住的问题
- 修复使用桌面快捷方式启动容器应用时无法启动的问题
# 常见问题说明
- 由于Termux-X11的渲染问题，在容器中使用"创建快捷方式"功能的时候会触发渲染错误，退出容器后重新启动即可解决，此问题并不影响快捷方式的创建
- 由于a8xx架构处理器将路径锁死，用户态没有权限读取GPU的实时数据，所以a8xx设备在使用MangoHud和安卓层面的性能监控的时候GPU占用会显示N/A，大部分a7xx设备都可以正常读取GPU占用率，因为我没有a6xx所以无法获取测试数据
- 在使用虚拟控件的过程中如果发现视角被限制无法移动，请在触控设置中打开"相对光标移动"选项

releases.name: Winlator-Glibc v1.0-RC1
releases.body:
# 说明

此发布包为 RC1 版本，作为 Winlator-Glibc 项目的第一个测试版。本项目基于[原 7.1.5-glibc 版本](https://github.com/longjunyu2/winlator)更新而来，我们决定将 glibc 版本独立出来作为新项目开发，因此软件已更名并重置版本号。

---

> **提示**：如果你之前已安装我们的 7.1.6-beta1 测试版本，建议替换为本发布页面的 v1-RC1 版本。7.1.6-beta1 将不再维护，我们不再使用 7.1.x 命名版本号，今后将基于 v1 版本长期更新与维护。

# 更新内容
- 添加Arm64ec架构的wine（10.14）
- 添加FEX-PE模拟
- 更新Box64-0.4.1和Box64-0.38
- 更新Turnip-26.1.0
- 更新DXVK-2.7.1
- 加入终端支持
- Gstreamer更新至1.28.1
- 加入Termux-x11的显示后端支持
# 常见问题说明
- 由于Winlator-Glibc的结构特殊性，目前仍无法实现与Winlator原版的共存
- 在原生x server的显示模式中部分wine会出现虚拟控件无法使用的情况，解决办法是去到设置界面启用Termux-x11的显示模式
- 使用Termux-x11显示模式时如果遇到视角卡死受限的情况请在操控选项中启用相对光标移动
- 编辑容器中的"显示FPS"功能所展示的GPU占用性能数据是不准确的，仅供娱乐使用，由于我们无法找到在设备未root的情况下能正常读取GPU数据的办法，所以此项功能仅仅只是基于已有数据推测，如果你需要准确的性能占用情况，请在容器中使用DXVK_HUD的变量开启性能监控
- Gstreamer在对部分游戏解码的时候仍存在问题，请等待正式版修复
- Turnip-26.1.0驱动对于Snapdragon 8 Elite以上处理器的支持仍不完整，目前仅供测试使用

emulators.description: Atari ST 与 STE 模拟器，68000 核心精确对齐周期。

releases.name: NeoST 0.6.5
releases.body:
## NeoST 0.6.5

Rewind, a cleaner Shifter and DMA sound, smoother audio recovery, and many usability fixes.

Try it in the browser, nothing to install: **[habib256.github.io/neost](https://habib256.github.io/neost/)**.

**What's new**
- **Rewind**: Ctrl+Alt+R steps back in time, floppies included (off by default).
- **Accuracy**: Closure runs clean (no stray black frames, no flickering borders); STE DMA sound, Shifter hardscroll, IKBD and serial chips closer to the real hardware; selectable master crystal.
- **Games**: Lemmings, Pacemaker, Obsession and Extase join the games replayed against Hatari (27 in total); TOS 1.06 US boots.
- **Usability**: picking a machine model also picks a matching TOS, and picking a TOS adjusts the model; a quieter terminal (`--verbose` for the full log); adaptive zoom fixed on Enchanted Land; a warm reset or a config change no longer scrambles Spectrum 512 pictures; twelve more keyboard layouts; keyboard joystick fires with right Alt/Option instead of right Ctrl (MacBooks have none); joystick dongles offered only on the port their game reads; bitmap explorer in the debugger; MIDI split and Time Code.

releases.name: NeoST 0.6.4
releases.body:
## NeoST 0.6.4

**What's new**
- **Accuracy**: MFP timers start on their own clock edge (Lethal Xcess on STE gets its top border back); MFP, ACIA, SCC and WD1772 closer to their datasheets.
- **Mouse**: drag-and-drop works in games and on the desktop; Chessmaster is now playable.
- **Games**: Lethal Xcess, Golden Axe, Rick Dangerous and Pang join the games replayed against Hatari (23 in total).
- **Verification**: a wider regression net (reference screens, game replays, the whole disk collection, Mega STE at 16 MHz) and a 68000 bench that now covers bus errors and double faults.

**Save states**: format v59, unchanged since 0.6.3.

Packages contain no Atari ROM: EmuTOS is the default. Licences included.

releases.name: NeoST 0.6.3 — NetUSBee USB and built-in networking
releases.body:
## NeoST 0.6.3 — NetUSBee USB and built-in networking

- **NetUSBee USB devices:** connect a virtual USB keyboard, mouse or disk image
  to either port. Hot-plug devices in Configuration → Network, save them in
  profiles, or use `--usb1` / `--usb2` in the headless runner. USB4TOS drivers
  have been tested with keyboard input, mouse packets and file reads/writes.
  Disk images support read-only mounting. Native ST-side USB drivers are required.
- **Built-in NAT:** IPv4/IPv6 networking without libslirp or GLib, including
  DHCP, DNS, TCP/UDP and explicit port forwarding. STinG/ENEC can load HTTP pages.
- **Hardware accuracy:** further CPU, video, floppy, serial and sound fixes,
  backed by chip documentation and regression benches. Vroom Elite starts on STE.
- **Issue #44:** missing Atari ROMs are reported as skipped Spectrum 512 tests;
  available machines still detect regressions, and partial runs cannot overwrite
  the reference set.

**Save states use format v59. Older states cannot be loaded.** Disk image contents
remain external to save states. USB passthrough and isochronous transfers are not
implemented.

releases.name: NeoST 0.6.2
releases.body:
## NeoST 0.6.2 — closer to the metal

Seven weeks of hardware fidelity work since 0.6.1.

**Deterministic external control.** A `--server` mode, joystick scripts, memory probes
and state exploration: the same script replays the same game down to the cycle. Disks
can be swapped while running and drive B unplugged from the server.

**Serial and keyboard chips rebuilt to match the hardware.** The MFP USART, the Mega STE
SCC, the MIDI and keyboard ACIAs, the IKBD protocol and the real-time clock. Custom 6301
keyboard programs are now recognised: *Froggies over the Fence* runs on all three disks.

**Floppies and hard disks.** More faithful STX copy protections, WD1772 write-protect
timing, and ACSI transfers that honour the DMA sector count.

**68881 FPU.** Transcendental functions are bit-exact.

**Video and memory.** STE 336-pixel mode, the 22-bit video counter wrap, the
"stopped Shifter" trick (resolution 3), and two new RAM sizes: 2176 KB and 2.5 MB.

**Sound.** The PSG crackle in *Super Hang-On* is gone, and STE DMA sound starts on the
exact sample of the PLAY write.

**Comfort.** Alt+Enter toggles fullscreen with mouse capture, mouse sensitivity is

releases.name: NeoST 0.6.1
releases.body:
## NeoST 0.6.1 — your settings stay put

A patch release. No new features: **23 defects** found and fixed across five rounds of multi-agent bug hunting, plus a hardware-validation pass on the published packages.

### Settings are saved again

On macOS and on every AppImage, NeoST runs from **read-only media**, so it stores its configuration in your user directory — but it never created that directory, and every setting was silently lost when you closed the emulator. **Five of the eight packages were affected.** Machine profile, video, audio and MIDI setup now survive a restart.

### Also fixed

- **The macOS disk image installs by drag and drop.** It shipped with the app alone, no `Applications` shortcut.
- **The web build ships its licences** (GPL-3.0, GPL-2.0, third-party notices), like every other package.
- **A save-state can no longer be reloaded under a different ROM.** The pairing relied on two bytes of TOS version, which five localisations share, so resuming under the wrong ROM froze the CPU without a word. The state format is now **v19**; v18 and older are refused explicitly, with a message that says why.

releases.name: Ryujinx-Nextendo 1.10.2
releases.body:
## Mario Kart 8 Deluxe online fixed (2306-0502)
- 1.10.0 started deferring every Bsd poll with a finite timeout. That broke the NEX connection of Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, which failed with error 2306-0502. MK8's ordinary NEX polls now use the blocking path again, as in 1.9.9; eventfd polls and the finite-timeout optimization of other games (Portal 2 and others) are unchanged (#75)

## New online games
- SpeedRunners 2: Nextendo routes scoped to the game, and a TLS peer reset during the handshake is now returned to the game as an SSL error instead of stopping the emulator (#79)
- Just Dance 2022: Nextendo routes, exact-build TLS trust patch with native certificate verification kept on, and blocking UDP receives no longer hold the shared socket thread (#74)

emulators.latest_body:
What's new in 0.78

For players
- **32-bit devices:** one APK now holds both ARMv8 (arm64-v8a) and ARMv7
  (armeabi-v7a). Android picks the right one on install, so 64-bit devices
  always run the 64-bit version. OpenGL ES 3.0 is still required.
- **Screen orientation:** the setting now applies to the launcher as well as
  the game and takes effect at once. Auto respects the system rotation lock.
- **Sound:** the audio buffer margin now adapts to the device.
- **Launcher:** new Advanced screen with a Debug mode switch. With it off,
  nothing is written to the log.
- **Logs:** new screen under Data to export, share or send logs to the
  developer, or clear them.

Under the hood
- **Most of the game is now ported C++:** - game code is moving from recompiled to ported native ARM code.
- **Old processor code removed:** x87 emulation is gone from the generated
  code, and the whole game runs in 24-bit floating point. MMX, CPU detection
  and the Pentium FDIV workarounds are removed too.

Known limits
- ARMv7 has only been tested in the 32-bit mode of a 64-bit phone, not on a
  real 32-bit device, so speed on older hardware is unknown.

releases.name: v0.77
releases.body:
What's new:

### For players
- **Dynamic Fullscreen for races.** A new Screen Size option that fits the race to your phone's shape (20:9, 16:9, tablets) with no black bars, you can find it in Resolution tabs in-game Graphics settings. The view widens to the sides and the HUD keeps its proportions. It is the default for new imports. 
- **Options on the first screen.** The "NFS Web Site" button is now "Options...", so the settings are one tap away.
- **Gamepads: Analog or Digital** (Controls → Gamepads). In Digital mode you steer with the D-pad and use the triggers for gas and brake, like a keyboard.
- **Force feedback: one choice, Off / Phone / Gamepad**, instead of two separate switches. The in-game Stick Volume slider now actually sets the vibration strength (it used to always be full).
- **Dead zone and saturation** from the game's own Dead Zone screen now work, separately for the stick and each trigger.
- **The demo movie no longer freezes** on its last frame.
- **Split screen** uses the Modern Patch layout.

### Under the hood (same behaviour, now native code instead of recompiled)

releases.name: v0.76
releases.body:
What's new:

- New launcher UI on Compose.
- Network races work: phone with phone over Wi-Fi (IPX or TCP/IP), and phone with a PC running the Modern Patch over TCP/IP, as host or client.
- Disc image import: the launcher reads the game straight from an ISO or BIN/CUE image, on the first start and on the Data screen.
- Faster and cooler: the renderer driver and about fifty of the game's heaviest functions now run as native code. Each was checked bit for bit against the original. Removed voodoo2a emulation wrapper - now GPU code is fully native OpenGLES. 
- Rear-view mirror like the main view: full draw distance, track detail, full-size cars, sky with clouds and lightning, car lights and headlights.
- Fixed bugs on certain devices with saves.

emulators.description: NES 模拟器，把游戏画面渲染为 3D 场景。
emulators.latest_body:
This one is mostly about what happens *under* the 3D. The emulator itself got a lot better.

## New

**Accuracy: 147 of 147 on AccuracyCoin.** 0.5.0 passed 128. Zaxnes was also compared cycle by cycle with a transistor-level simulation of the NES chips (421,901 CPU cycles, DMA included), and the timing matched. Where the two still differ, tests made on real consoles side with Zaxnes.

**Over 400 mappers.** Up from 144. That includes the **Famicom Disk System**, the **VS. System** with its cabinet buttons, and newer boards like the Rainbow.

**A fast core.** It skips work the screen doesn't need, but gives the same results as the accurate core. We checked that frame by frame on 320 ROMs. Handhelds use it by default.

**New options window.** One slider goes from *Fastest* to *Most faithful* and sets everything that costs speed. A simple mode shows only what most people need, and an advanced mode shows everything. It works the same on the PC and on the console screen.

releases.name: Zaxnes 0.5.0
releases.body:
Zaxnes is an independent project, not affiliated with Geod Studio or Nintendo.

## Highlights

**3dSen 2.0 and 2.1 compatibility.** Profiles from 3dSen 2.0 and 2.1 import and play, with what the new versions brought: reflections, bend, the new camera and Lua features.

**A real NES emulator, not just a gimmick.** Mapper support goes from 85 to 144, and AccuracyCoin from 89 to 128 tests out of 147. More accuracy work is coming in the next releases.

**New widescreen hacks: Kirby's Adventure and Faxanadu.** Every regional version of each. Faxanadu already has its 3D profile in this release; Kirby's is on the way.

**Smooth scrolling at 120 Hz (experimental).** On a 120 Hz screen, the playfield is drawn between two emulated frames, from the run-ahead.

**RetroArch shaders.** Slang shaders (through librashader) on the Vulkan / DirectX 12 renderer: CRT, scanlines, LCD, Mega Bezel TV frames. A pack of presets is built in, separately for 2D and 3D. Available on Android too.

**Editor mode for 3D profiles (work in progress).** An AI-assisted editor: it gives an AI agent a harness through a local MCP server, and a prompt ready to copy and paste. Expect more on it in the next release.

# Zaxnes 0.4.1

Independent project, not affiliated with Geod Studio or Nintendo. NES is a trademark of Nintendo.

Widescreen fixes.

## Ninja Gaiden III

- The enemies, lanterns and items the game places on the screen when the camera reaches them now wait in the margins, where they will appear, instead of popping in at the edge of the 4:3 picture.

## All games

- In the widescreen margins, a sprite behind the background hides the sprites of lower priority there, as the NES does.

releases.name: Zaxnes 0.4.0
releases.body:
# Zaxnes 0.4.0

Independent project, not affiliated with Geod Studio or Nintendo. NES is a trademark of Nintendo.

## New

- **Widescreen.** Games made for it, or patched for it, draw past the 256 pixels of the NES picture, in 2D and in 3D. Built-in widescreen hacks for Zelda II, Mega Man 1 to 6, Super Mario Bros., Super Mario Bros. 3, Castlevania, Ninja Gaiden III, Adventure Island, Excitebike, Final Fantasy, Blaster Master, Metroid and Metal Force (Korea), each in a plain and an advanced mode (objects and enemies shown in the margins). The hacks are found by the ROM's signatures, so other builds (Europe, Japan) of these games are covered where a pack exists. A *WideScreen & Hacks* screen per game shows how well the ROM fits, part by part, and offers each hack's options (*No slowdown*, *Invincible*, level select where the game has one).

- **Console mode on the desktop** (F1 or Home): the handheld interface with the mouse, the keyboard or a pad; the desktop now opens on its ROM list.

Release Notes for openMSX 22.0 (2026-10-28)
===========================================

Thanks to many contributors (who make good use of modern AI tools), we
have a very long list of changes again. Major features are found in the
debugger GUI, with a new Raster Beam Viewer and Tracer functionality. We also
have the Quick Setup Editor, for one-window access to all major setup
settings.

Then AI hit us with dozens of Pull Requests with new and improved
functionality... Not all purely AI-generated, but also using AI to analyse
bulk measurements. This led to many VDP accuracy improvements and emulation of
new devices like plotters, Panasonic FS-JH1 Joy Handle steering wheel (that
came with Konami's A1 Spirit), light guns, Franky, Makoto, SD Mapper V1 and
SM-X WiFi. There's even a synthetic TCP/IP UNAPI device to be able to try out
network programs in openMSX.

And many, many more things...

Special thanks to all the contributors of this release who are not in the core
team! Keep those pull requests coming!

Here's the list with all highlights and details:

MSX device support:
- fixed Yamanooto SCC register visibility

releases.name: openMSX 21.0
releases.body:
openMSX 21.0 has many improvements on the new GUI introduced in openMSX 20.0 (especially the debugger) and several other smaller features. It also introduces the "setups" concept, which enables you to define an MSX setup (e.g. a Philips VG 8020 with an external disk drive and a joystick, data recorder and printer connected). These can be created, loaded, and automatically started. They can also be saved automatically when you exit.

Furthermore, flash chip emulation has become a lot more accurate, thanks to Laurens Holst.

releases.name: openMSX 20.0
releases.body:
openMSX 20.0—Autumn Spring—is a major release, in which we introduce the new Graphical User Interface, replacing the OSD menu. A faster and more powerful debugger is now included in openMSX itself. Configuration for MSX joystick/JoyMega has been improved drastically using the new GUI. If you still want to use Catapult, you can use the Catapult release that came with openMSX 19.0. Please [read the release notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openMSX/openMSX/RELEASE_20_0/doc/release-notes.txt) for details of the openMSX changes.

As always, special thanks to all the contributors of this release who are not in the core team! Keep these pull requests coming!

Please note that as of now, a system with OpenGL 2 support is required to run openMSX.

releases.name: openMSX 19.1
releases.body:
openMSX 19.1—Reflection—is a bug fix release for openMSX 19.0, as we found some rather nasty issues after releasing, mostly that LaserDisc support was broken. No new Catapult will be released, as it has no changes.  Please [read the release notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openMSX/openMSX/RELEASE_19_1/doc/release-notes.txt) for details of the openMSX changes.

Thanks for those who gave us the feedback so that we found out about these issues.

Please note that this will be the last openMSX release that supports systems without OpenGL 2 or higher.

Pikmin 2 gets its original blob shadows back, the sticks and throws in

packs and maps carry over.

**Updating:** press **Update** in your launcher. On Android, install the new
APK over the old one. **Do not uninstall first**, or your data is lost.

**macOS:** there is no ready-made macOS download. Each player builds it
from source with `scripts/build-macos.sh` (see the macOS section of the
README).

  again.
* **Raised Pikmin limit:** more than 110 Pikmin latching onto the same enemy
  or treasure no longer crashes the game (#258).
* **Touch (Android):** the touch controls no longer break after leaving a
  cave or area (#238).

releases.name: Open Nectar 1.0.9.1 — Windows ONLY antivirus fix
releases.body:
# Open Nectar 1.0.9.1 — Windows antivirus fix

### **Windows only.** 

Linux, macOS and Android stay on
[1.0.9](https://github.com/SSunnKing/Open-Nectar---Pikmin-Native-PC-Mobile-Port/releases/tag/1.0.9).
Download those from there. Nothing changes in the games themselves.

**Updating:** press **Update** in your launcher. Saves, settings and texture
packs carry over.

## Windows Defender flagged the launcher as a trojan

Some players got a "Threat found" warning from Windows Defender for
`nectar-launcher.exe` (`Trojan:Win32/Bearfoos.A!ml`). This was a false
positive. The `!ml` means it came from Defender's machine-learning guess,
not from a real malware match.

The launcher was doing things that look suspicious to an antivirus: it
started `curl.exe` and `tar.exe` in the background to download updates and
texture packs, and the exe had no publisher or version info. This release
changes that:

* Downloads now happen inside the launcher instead of through `curl.exe`.
* Update zips are unpacked inside the launcher instead of through `tar.exe`.
* `nectar.exe`, `nectar-pal.exe` and `nectar-launcher.exe` now have
  publisher and version information (right-click → Properties → Details).

releases.name: Playden for PS5 0.12.0-beta.2
releases.body:
Games can now use the controller's or a headset's microphone for voice chat. Older Japanese games can get a Japanese system locale. New runtime kit 0.31 brings both.

Beta 2 also adds a Compatibility filter from the community's compatibility list, keeps the artwork you set with ArtSwap, and makes installs 337 MB smaller. A DualShock 4 bridged by PoorDS4 drives Playden and games, and Chicory: A Colorful Tale and UNBEATABLE can be installed again.

> [!WARNING]
> Beta of alpha software. Betas can have new bugs. Playden signs in to your real Steam account and reads and writes your Steam Cloud saves. Read [Before you use it](https://github.com/leolobato/playden-ps5#before-you-use-it) first.

## Downloads

| File | What it is |

| `playden-kit-0.31.zip` | Runtime kit 0.31. Playden downloads it by itself; you need this file only to install the kit by hand. |

releases.name: Playden for PS5 0.12.0-beta.1
releases.body:
Online play is here, for everyone who wants to try it. Set a game to Online and Playden runs Valve's own Steam client next to it on the PS5, signed in as you, so the game reaches official servers, Steam lobbies and your Steam friends as on a PC. It is experimental, chosen per game, and off by default.

Beta 1 also brings GOG as a second store, Steam collections in the Library, a regrouped Settings, and new runtime kit 0.29, which fixes Unreal Engine 5 games on Direct3D 12 that stopped with "Fatal error!".

> [!WARNING]
> Beta of alpha software. Betas can have new bugs. Playden signs in to your real Steam account and reads and writes your Steam Cloud saves. Online play signs that account in to Steam from the console, and a game with Valve Anti-Cheat could get it banned from that game. Read [Before you use it](https://github.com/leolobato/playden-ps5#before-you-use-it) and [Online play](https://github.com/leolobato/playden-ps5/blob/main/docs/online-play.md) first.

releases.name: Pocket2Droid v1.0.2
releases.body:
Pocket2Droid 1.0.2 adds Windows Mobile 5.0 support, Internet access and more customization.

- **Windows Mobile 5.0:** Added support for compatible Device Emulator ROM images.
- **Internet access:** Connect to the Internet inside Windows Mobile through your Android device’s connection. Internet access is enabled by default for new ROM profiles.
- **If Internet access doesn’t work:** Make sure Internet access is **On** in Pocket2Droid’s ROM settings. Inside Windows Mobile, open **Network Cards** settings and change **“My network card connects to”** from **Work** to **The Internet**. Tap **OK**, then try browsing again. Some network configurations still require manual setup, and older browsers may not support modern HTTPS websites.
- **Custom resolutions:** Set your own guest screen width and height alongside the existing presets. Compatibility varies by ROM. Custom resolutions may cause display glitches or require touchscreen recalibration inside Windows Mobile.
- **Restart option:** Restart Windows Mobile directly from the session menu.
- **Per-ROM StorageCard folders:** Choose a separate StorageCard folder for each ROM while keeping the general StorageCard folder unchanged.

releases.name: Pocket2Droid v1.0.1 — First Public Release
releases.body:
First public release of Pocket2Droid, a Windows Mobile emulator for Android that runs the complete operating system, including compatible applications and games.

### Features
- ROM library with individual settings and persistent storage.
- Shared StorageCard folder with file importing.
- On-screen controls with adjustable transparency, vibration feedback and multi-key support.
- Global button mapping for keyboards and wired/Bluetooth controllers, including sticks and triggers.
- Display scaling, orientation, screen position and fullscreen options.

### Requirements
- ARM64 Android device running Android 7.0 or newer.
- A compatible Windows Mobile `.bin` ROM.

ROMs, games and applications are not included.

### Getting started
1. Install the APK attached below.
2. Open Pocket2Droid and grant storage access.
3. Tap **+ → PPC Rom** to import your ROM.
4. Tap the ROM to start Windows Mobile.

To copy files into the guest’s storage card, use **+ → File to StorageCard**.

### Please note
- Compatibility and performance vary by device, ROM and game.

[Discord](https://discord.gg/cVHYSwn9Bq) · [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@Pocket2Droid)

## What's New - controller support tested and working on both platforms for gameplay, test out the app on your android handhelds now! - fixed rescan library on every home page visit - added manual rescan library to settings (try this if 1.6 messed with your library) - added pull from top to refresh in library. - File transparency: All app files will be stored in 'Documents/Pocket8' for Android and 'On My iPhone > Pocket8' for iOS. - (android) added import existing folder for those with existing game libraries. this indexes the game locations from your external folders to the app's library. - added file/library cleaning settings: clear external games, factory reset library. - fixes to controller support on home page- should be fully navigable with controller. - css optimizations for dpad, attempting to address issue #16 but still need feedback for those on older iOS hardware. - visual branding updates to align with PICO-8 licensing and aesthetics

releases.name: v1.6 - Gamepad (Setup), QoL, UI
releases.body:
**KNOWN ISSUE:** Physical controllers are currently still broken in this build. Directory fixes are working. Recommended for touch-screen users only

Hey everyone, v1.6 is live.

I got a hold of an Android device to test with, which brought a lot of bugs to my immediate attention. I’ve done some work cleaning up the codebase to make this actually usable on devices like the Retroid, Thor, Ayaneo.

Just to be transparent: Since I'm working with Zep on the official iOS release, the Android version is going to remain an unofficial side project. However, I still want it to be a quality experience for those of you using it, so I'm pushing these QoL updates to get it stable.

**The Big Fixes:**

**Android Storage Fixed:** Closed issue #18. The directory picker now actually works. You can point it to your external SD card or any ROM folder, and it won't crash or fail to import. It respects your folder structure and keeps the app data separate.

**Immersive Mode:** Closed issue #19. The Android navigation bar now hides correctly, giving you full-screen real estate for the games. There's also a setting to remove the virtual controls completely for a true full screen mode.

[[IMPORTANT]] Android has been sunsetted until further notice. see [the future of pocket8.](https://www.reddit.com/r/Pocket8/comments/1rerp4t/the_future_of_pocket8_important/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=web3x&utm_name=web3xcss&utm_term=1&utm_content=share_button) One of my biggest updates so far. Pocket8 is now officially running on Android! **New Features:** - **Android Support:** There was a huge demand for this. I'm listening! I don't have an Android device to test on currently, so please leave feedback. - **Multicart Support:** .p8.png Multi-Cart titles are now supported. **Note: .p8 Multi-Cart titles are not.** The current engine is a web-build, and does not usually support .p8 files or multicart titles at all. However, games that use absolute file names when loading carts in their code work fine. An example of a working multicart game is [Golf Monday](https://johanpeitz.itch.io/golf-monday). - **Library Management:** You can now rename and favorite your carts. Long-press to organize your collection.

**Coming Soon:**

emulators.latest_body:
## Security: Steam token redaction in logs

GameHub Lite 5.1.8 fixes a logging issue where Steam authentication-related values could appear in diagnostic logs. 
In some cases, logs could include fields such as `steamToken`, `refreshToken`, or `accessToken` from Steam login/launch flows.

**Publicly posted logs containing these fields should be deleted or redacted.**

### IMPORTANT

This should go without saying but If you find any security issues, please reach out **PRIVATELY**. 
I have not checked if this issue is still present in recent GameHub versions, already ruined my one day off I was spending with my family by the person who reported this publicly and I do not plan on spending any more time on this.

### Changelog

The fix adds centralized log redaction for Steam/auth token fields, Steam QR login URLs, JWT-like token strings, and launch command token arguments before logs are written. This covers the app loggers, JavaSteam logging, and the PC launch-log file writer.

This release also pins local patch builds to `apktool 2.12.1`

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Producdevity/gamehub-lite/compare/v5.1.7...v5.1.8

releases.body:
Frame generation (thank you The412Banner for your contribution.

This was the first (and last) contribution made with AI. Very thankful that Banner had the patience to deal with the amount of changes we requested for this to get merged. That said, future AI PR's will be closed automatically (and have been closed). Many are not willing to put in the effort that Banner did and I don't have the energy to review everything. **If it is not worth writing/understanding the code, it is not worth reviewing the code.**

### App changes

  - Added AI Frame Generation toggle + gear settings dialog to the in-game sidebar (Performance tab).
  - 6 presets (Eco, Flow, Balanced, Boost, Clear, Max) and a flow-scale slider with live feedback.
  - Settings persist to SharedPreferences and re-apply on every `WineActivity.onCreate`/`onResume`.
  - Added a Vulkan ICD JSON writer so the framegen driver hooks correctly across all 5 package variants.
  - Fixed `Locale.ROOT` formatting for float values to avoid comma-decimal issues on non-English locales.
  - Fixed try/catch label collision in WineActivity smali patch — apktool rebuild now fails loudly on errors.

releases.name: GameHub Lite v5.1.6
releases.body:
# GameHub Lite v5.1.6

This release fixes an actual app-side launch issue, and yes, also exists because apparently backend fixes do not count unless there is a fresh APK attached to a GitHub release.

The main app fix is for devices where GameHub would silently refuse to launch games when the `getUnknownDevices` / `startType` API path returned a `404`. Instead of failing closed and doing absolutely nothing, the app now falls back like it already did for the no-internet path.

Confirmed affected and fixed:

- AYANEO Pocket FIT
- Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 / Adreno 750
- Android 14

### Backend changes

More work happened in [gamehub-lite-api](https://github.com/Producdevity/gamehub-lite-api), because that is where a lot of compatibility and component delivery work lives now.

Backend changes since the `v5.1.5` release include:

- Updated simulator response timestamps so stale responses get refreshed.
- Added release asset verification and MD5 checks for GitHub release assets.
- Updated component manifests, timestamps, deprecated component removal, and total counts.
- Cleaned up SteamAgent2 manifest naming.
- Removed drivers that were already added in the latest GameHub manifest.

releases.name: GameHub Lite v5.1.5
releases.body:
This release is mainly here to make the backend work visible and add the addition off Japanese app translations, thank you @reindex-ot for your contribution!

Most of the recent fixes and updates happened server-side in the GameHub Lite backend, so existing installs already benefited without needing a new APK. Apparently that makes it look like nothing happened, so here is an app release too. I will make a useless release every time we improve something that gets served via the server. 

### Backend changes

The main work happened in:

- [gamehub-lite-api](https://github.com/Producdevity/gamehub-lite-api)
- [gamehub-lite-worker](https://github.com/Producdevity/gamehub-lite-worker)

Recent backend-side work includes updated component manifests, new/updated container components, imagefs updates, corrected component counts, proxy/URL updates, and fixes around component list handling.

In particular, the worker/API side is where most compatibility and content fixes now happen. If something starts working without an APK update, that is why.

### App changes

- Added Japanese translation updates.
- Added/updated Japanese project documentation.
- Update apktool to 2.12.1

releases.body:
GameHub Lite adds **RTS Touch Controls**. 

Massive thanks to @Nightwalker743 for their contributions!

**Changelogs**
- Add RTS Touch Controls - @Nightwalker743 
- Improve stability of `patch.sh` script - @sgumil 
- add APK build GitHub workflow  - @ObfuscatedVoid 

**RTS Controls feature list:**

**_Tap to Click_** - Tap anywhere to move cursor and click (Like move cursor to touchpoint on Winlator)
**_Drag for Box Selection_** - Drag finger to create selection box (left mouse button held during drag)
**_Long Press for Right-Click_** - Hold finger for 300ms to trigger right-click
**_Double-Tap for Double-Click_** - Tap twice within 250ms and 50 pixels to double-click
**_Two-Finger Pan for Camera_** - Drag with two fingers to pan camera
**_Pinch-to-Zoom_*** - Pinch two fingers inward to zoom out, pinch outward to zoom in (mouse wheel scroll)
**_Toggle Switch_*** - Enable/disable RTS controls in Settings > Controls tab (in the side overlay menu when you're in a game).

_The two gestures that have an asterisk can be customized in the RTS Gesture Settings menu._

This alpha keeps each game in a folder of its own with everything that belongs to it, gives cheats their own list, adds a speed limit and a second frame generation method, and fixes a lost graphics device and black boxes that spread over the picture. Performance and compatibility still vary by game.

### New and improved

- **One folder per game.** A game can sit in a folder of its own in `roms/`, together with its update and DLC files, its mods (`mods/`), its cheats (`cheats/`) and its own post-processing presets (`reshade/`). ProsperoEden tells the game from its update and DLC by what each file holds, so the files can have any names. **Delete from console** removes the folder's update and DLC too. Games downloaded from a source now go into a folder of their own the same way. Your files stay where they are and keep working. See [Game files folder](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md#game-files-folder).
- **Cheats in a list of their own.** A game's settings have a **Cheats** row next to **Mods**: every cheat of the game with its own switch, and an **All cheats** switch apart from the Mods one. **Mods** now lists patches and replacement files

releases.name: ProsperoEden v1.003.000
releases.body:
This alpha focuses on mod stability, controller support, graphics correctness and lower emulation overhead. Performance and compatibility still vary by game; these changes do not guarantee a particular frame rate.

### Fixes and improvements

- **TOTK + UltraCam startup crash fixed.** Large modded RomFS rebuilds could overflow the filesystem thread stack during cleanup and close the whole app. Cleanup is now iterative. Tested with TOTK **1.1.1** and an older UltraCam mod: the game reached its menu, and the user confirmed the free camera works in gameplay. Game/mod versions still need to match; this is not a claim that every UltraCam version or TOTK update works.
- **Memory size per game.** Choose 4, 6 or 8 GiB of emulated console memory under **Settings > Performance > Memory**, with game-specific overrides for demanding mods. This uses the PS5's existing shared memory pool; it does not add physical RAM. See [Console memory](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/blob/v1.003.000/docs/SETTINGS.md#console-memory).
- **DualSense audio haptics.** HD rumble can use the controller's audio haptics path, with lifecycle and failure handling fixes.
- **Touchpad and controls.** Spl

releases.name: ProsperoEden v1.002.000
releases.body:
- **More free memory for demanding games.** The console's memory is one pool shared by the emulated console, the emulator itself and the graphics, and part of it was held without being used. The emulated console's memory, the code caches and a reserve on the system's side now take memory only when they need it. A large open-world game at 2x has about 3.5 GiB free during play instead of 2.2 GiB, at the same frame rate, so a long session runs out of memory far later.
- **PS5 Pro memory mode.** On a PS5 Pro, ProsperoEden asks for the larger memory pool the console offers: 13.5 GiB instead of 12 GiB. A line at launch (`memory:` in `stderr.log`) says whether it is active. Contributed by [OverkillLabs](https://github.com/OverkillLabs3).
- **"Ran out of graphics memory" less often above 1x.** The part that frees textures no game is using could stop looking before it had freed anything, so graphics memory filled up although much of it could be freed. Contributed by [mzet97](https://github.com/mzet97).
- **Vibration strength (new setting).** **Settings > Controls > Vibration strength** sets how strong the DualSense vibrates: 25%, 50%, 75% or 100% of what a game asks for. The controller answ

releases.name: ProsperoEden v1.001.000
releases.body:
- **A new launcher.** The menu was rebuilt. Five sections sit on a rail at the left (Home, Library, Multiplayer, Settings, About): L1 and R1 go from one to the next, and Left from a screen's edge opens the rail. Home is built around the game to continue, with its cover and what it runs with. The Library shows your games as covers, with the chosen game's details beside them. A game's settings are a page of their own, and Settings is a board of tiles.
- **Themes.** The launcher's look is a theme, chosen in **Settings > Theme**. This version comes with one, Canopy; [docs/THEMES.md](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/blob/main/docs/THEMES.md) says what a theme is made of.
- **An opening.** ProsperoEden appears out of the console's own launch picture without a cut: its mark comes forward over the picture, then goes to its place as the menu arrives. Any button skips it, and it plays only when the app is started.

## Changelog
### New features & non-bug fix changes
- Made the analog camera more responsive and less sluggish
- Extended the draw distance for some actors:
  - These actors tend to be non-enemy actors, since loading those from too far away can cause sigkill errors
- Disabled draw distance extension for melon crates
- Made the first person inversion option apply to Gyro & mouse controls
- Added in the ability to boot recomp via a CLI argument ( #55 )

### Bug Fixes
- Fixed an issue where a large spike in CPU load would permanently kill the audio engine until a program restart.
- Fixed an issue where disabled lightning would not work for some lightning events ( #30 )
- Fixed an issue where the game would leave zipper marks on the game during the open zipper animation
- Fixed an issue where the main menu scrolling background would look very weird on expanded HUD ( #42 )

releases.name: recomp-launcher 0.3.0
releases.body:
### Added
- The installer shows its version (the game's tag, or the short commit for a
  build off a branch) in the window's corner and title, and on start asks
  GitHub for the game's newest release: a newer one gets a download button.
  Offline it says nothing.
- `game.files` takes globs: `*.iso` makes a folder holding a disc image the
  game, for a title whose setup takes an image rather than an install.
- `installer.yml` takes `platforms` (default `windows linux macos`), so a
  Windows-only game doesn't publish installers that can't build it.
- A `game.files` entry may be alternatives, `a|b`: `HOVER.EXE|hover*.zip` is
  the game's folder or a folder holding a zip of it.

- The Windows installer carries version info and a manifest, and a release
  has `SHA256SUMS.txt`, so antivirus heuristics and players can check it.
- A log of why the installer stopped (`%APPDATA%\recomp-launcher\launcher.log`
  on Windows), and an error box instead of the window vanishing.

### Fixed
- On Windows a step line after a blank line was glued to the line before it
  (ConPTY skips the blank line with a cursor move), so the bar missed that step.

releases.name: recomp-launcher 0.2.0
releases.body: One installer per game instead of one launcher for every game. A game repo adds `launcher/launcher.json` and calls `.github/workflows/installer.yml`; see the README's *Adding a game* and the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md). The first game: [redalert2-recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/redalert2-recomp/releases).

# CronyX v3 

## 🆕 New Features

- CronyFG — experimental own native frame generation engine.

- Screen Stretch slider (0–100%) in screen effects — smooth stretching instead of hard full-stretch.

- Removed forced sharpening when stretching — effects are now controlled only from the effects menu.

- In-game virtual buttons editor over the running game: add/move/delete, change theme, assign keys — without leaving the game.

- New MangoHud-style FPS counter theme available for selection.

- Fixed horizontal FPS counter mode — it now uses the full screen width.

- Move a game to another container with automatic save transfer via the ludusavi index (20k+ games) and an option to manually pick the save folder.

- Auto-search for .exe files in Downloads folders — import your apps in one tap.

- Smart game title detection taken from Bannerlator (steam_appid, GOG manifests, exe PE metadata) with SteamGridDB cover matching.

- 9 on-screen button styles from WinNative (Glass, Shadow, Slate, Halo, Glint, Reticle, Neon, Lumina…) + a palette of 10 accent colors; old .icp profiles load without migration.

# Release notes — 67956fb..ad04ac3 (27 commits)

**Project renamed!** The project has been renamed from **Winlator ref4ik** to **CronyX** — the app will now appear under the new name. All previous versions were released under the name **Winlator ref4ik**, but from now on the project will be called **CronyX**.

**What's New in This Version:**

- LSFG frame generation moved in-tree (`cpp/winlator/lsfg/` + DXBC): external `lsfg-vk-android` tree removed, `LsfgVkManager` replaced by `LsfgNative`
- LSFG HUD shows real→shown FPS pair with live armed state
- LSFG: SPIR-V cache pre-built on DLL import, apply without restart
- LSFG: adaptive output FPS target (WinNative parity), credits in About
- DRI3 AHB pixmaps: real size/stride, render pause for native scanout
- Vulkan effects: full-res offscreen buffer (swapchain size), fixed small-screen bug
- New Steam store: home/detail/search/catalog/news screens, prices/platforms/metascore, search suggest, full-text search with filters (jsoup)
- Steam library: content filter menu with counts, dedupe by appId
- Steam: fixed launch paths (workingDir/exe dir), download stall watchdog

Xbox Live through Insignia, and game fixes.

### Xbox Live
- **Insignia** — Settings → Network → Connection → Xbox Live: Insignia connects the console to Insignia, the revival of the original Xbox Live: Live games sign in, find matches and play online. If your Internet provider blocks Insignia's DNS server, point it at a computer running insigniaDNS instead
- **Xbox Live setup** — Settings → Network → Xbox Live setup walks you through it, one step at a time: the connection, the Xbox dashboard, registering the console with Insignia's Setup Assistant (downloaded for you), then making or recovering your account in the dashboard
- **Dashboard** — the library's Dashboard button (top left) starts the Xbox dashboard from the console's hard disk, where Xbox Live accounts are made and recovered. The first time, it installs the dashboard from a zip of its files (dashboard 5960) that you provide: hakuX doesn't include one
- **Title updates** — a game's Xbox Live update, once downloaded, starts with the game. Forza Motorsport's 60 and 120 fps mods cover its update too

### Games
- **Fable: The Lost Chapters** — the hero's face and arms are no longer black or noise

releases.name: hakuX 1.2.0
releases.body:
System link, stability and compatibility improvements.

### Network
- **System link over your network** — Settings → Network → System link → LAN: hakuX devices on the same Wi-Fi network find each other as Xbox consoles on a LAN do. Devices the network's broadcasts don't reach, on another subnet or a VPN such as ZeroTier or Tailscale, are added by address under Other consoles
- **XLink Kai** — system link over the Internet through an XLink Kai engine running on a computer on your network; its web page picks the game's arena
- **Console identity** — each console has its own serial number, network address and online key. A device whose hard disk was copied from another one offers to make itself a new identity, since two consoles with one identity can't see each other


### Games
- **Sega GT 2002** — the cars have their paint, reflections and sun highlights
- **Doom 3** — no longer crashes as its main menu loads
- **Fatal Frame II** — starts and reads its disc in the order it asks for
- **AirForce Delta Storm** — answers the controller and the on-screen controls (it ignored all input)
- **Silent Hill 2** — no longer crashes when it loads a room

releases.name: hakuX 1.1.0
releases.body:
GPUs beyond Adreno (experimental).

### GPUs
- **Mali, Xclipse and PowerVR (experimental)** — hakuX runs on GPUs other than Adreno: features they lack are replaced (BC and 4444 textures decoded up front, standard border colours, the push block in a buffer, D32S8 depth), and known driver bugs are worked around (`hw/xbox/hle/vk/quirks.c`). Burnout 3 and Mercenaries run cleanly on a Pixel 8 (Mali-G715)
- **Vulkan 1.1 drivers** — GPUs whose drivers stop at Vulkan 1.1 (Valhall Mali on older or vendor-capped drivers, Qualcomm's own older drivers, early Xclipse, PowerVR BXM) run through a compatibility layer (`hw/xbox/hle/vk/compat.c`)
- **Older GPUs without descriptor indexing (experimental)** — Bifrost Mali (G71, G72, G76, G52) and PowerVR Rogue: each draw binds its own textures, and depth is clamped in the shader where the GPU can't
- **Adreno** — unchanged: every replacement is off where the GPU has the feature.

### App
- **GPU driver** — a screen of its own (Settings → GPU driver): the system driver and the stored packages in one list, with their versions and authors. Packages are checked when added and can be deleted (deleting the one in use goes back to the system driver)

releases.name: hakuX 1.0.0
releases.body:
A new core replaces xemu's QEMU-based one.

### New core
- **CPU** — the Xbox's x86 code runs on a FEX JIT (FEXCore fork), and the Xbox kernel is reimplemented natively (`native/kernel`): no QEMU
- **GPU** — the NV2A push buffer is decoded into Vulkan (HLE, `hw/xbox/hle`). Custom drivers (Turnip) load through adrenotools; driver-specific workarounds are quirks (`hw/xbox/hle/vk/quirks.c`, `debug.hakux.quirks`)
- **Audio** — the MCPX APU runs on the core's own services (`native/dev/apu`), out through AAudio
- **Savestates** — per game, in slots, with the hard disk's files
- **Mods and cheats** — per game, from `mods/` (library long-press "Mods & cheats"): XBE patches and replaced disc files; 60 and 120 fps mods for 13 games (`mods/README.md`, generators in `tools/mods`)
- **Controllers** — each physical controller routed to a player with its own mapping; the on-screen controller adds to player 1

### New features
- **Updates** — hakuX looks for a newer release on GitHub when it starts and on demand (Settings → Updates); one found shows its notes and installs from there
- **Frontends** — a game launched from ES-DE or another frontend returns to it when it closes

releases.body:
# EmuHub v0.2 ALPHA

> ⚠️ **Alpha notice**  
> This is an early preview. Some features may still be refined, but core functionality is stable. Please report any issues on the [Issues page](../../issues).

---

## ✨ What's changed
### New Download Manager
- Persistent download history – Completed downloads saved to SharedPreferences and reloaded on app start.
- Active downloads list – Shows filename, progress bar, percentage, and bytes downloaded/total.
- Completed downloads list – Shows filename, size, file path, date.
- Delete file functionality – Delete button with confirmation dialog; physically removes file from storage (works for MediaStore and SAF URIs).
- Unique IDs for downloads – Each completed download gets a UUID, preventing duplicate entries when deleting.
- Unique filename generation – Duplicate files automatically renamed with counter before extension (e.g., file (1).zip instead of file.zip (1)).
- Custom download folder – Settings screen allows user to pick any folder via Storage Access Framework (SAF). Default is Downloads.
- Download start toast – Short notification when a download begins.

releases.name: EmuHub-v0.1-ALPHA
releases.body:
# EmuHub v0.1 ALPHA – First Public Release

🎉 **Welcome to the first alpha release of EmuHub!**  
EmuHub is an open‑source Android application that helps you download and manage GPU drivers (Turnip, Qualcomm) and PC emulation components (Wine, Proton, DXVK, etc.) for Adreno‑powered devices.

> ⚠️ **Alpha notice**  
> This is an early preview. Some features may be incomplete, and you may encounter bugs. Please report any issues on the [Issues page](../../issues).

---

## ✨ What's included

- **Device detection** – Shows Android version, total RAM, GPU model, and Adreno series.
- **Turnip driver downloads**  
  - For Adreno 8xx: choose between **StevenMXZ** (official) and **whitebelyash** (experimental) sources.  
  - For Adreno 6xx/7xx: automatically uses the stable v26.x branch.
- **Qualcomm driver** – Official driver (v863.1) offered for Adreno 6xx/7xx devices.
- **Emulation components** – Download Wine, Proton, Box64, WOWBox64, DXVK, FEXCore, VKD3D from the [WinNative-Emu Components](https://github.com/WinNative-Emu/Components) repository.
- **Latest version auto‑selection** – All releases are sorted semantically (e.g. `2.7.1` > `1.5.5`) and the newest is preselected.

- **An archive written as it is.** The new option **Preserve single-game archives**, in the *Writing the files* frame of

RomSieve 1.2.0 sorts a whole pack of DATs in one pass, reads DATs straight from their ZIP, 7z or RAR archive, and can
filter the files missing from the DAT by their name. Your settings, profiles and journals stay as they are, and a sort
made with 1.1.x or 1.0.x can still be undone.

  the first DAT that knows it, and each DAT keeps its own convention, filters and 1G1R. A lot may mix the three
  conventions.
- **DATs in an archive.** The DAT field also takes a **ZIP, 7z or RAR archive**, as downloaded, read without

releases.name: RomSieve 1.1.1
releases.body:
RomSieve 1.1.1 fixes how 1G1R handles games on several floppy disks in the No-Intro DATs, such as those of the Acorn
Archimedes. Your settings, profiles and journals stay as they are, and a sort made with 1.1.0 or 1.0.x can still be
undone.

- **Floppy disk sets kept together.** The No-Intro DATs of floppy disks number the disks `(Disk 1)`, `(Disk 2)`...,
  sometimes with a label: `(Disk 1, Game Disk)`, `(Disk 2 - Courses)`. RomSieve did not read these names as disks of
  one set, so 1G1R could keep some disks of a game and leave out the others. The disks of a set are now kept or left

emulators.latest_body:
This release candidate completes support for the cheat instructions implemented by Eden's DMNT engine and improves cheat-file parsing and process targeting.

**This is a pre-release for testing before v0.1.1.** Feedback and reproducible bug reports are welcome. It includes all improvements from rc1 through rc7.

### What's new since rc7

- **Extended cheat instructions:** implemented register comparisons, register save/restore operations and masks, persistent static registers, process pause/resume, and debug logging, with all operand and addressing forms supported by Eden.
- **Cheat execution:** corrected nested if/else handling, loop decoding, arithmetic behavior, and handling of truncated or unknown instructions. Controller input is sampled once per execution so multiple button conditions see the same input state.
- **Cheat files and process targeting:** fixed parsing of names containing Unicode symbols or accents. Memory operations and pause/resume now target the process identified by the cheat metadata, with a cached non-owning process reference.

releases.name: Ruzu v0.1.1-rc7
releases.body:
This release candidate fixes several cheat-engine decoding errors, adds missing process-memory service calls, and addresses an applet command that caused some game to abort.

**This is a pre-release for testing before v0.1.1.** Feedback and reproducible bug reports are welcome. It includes all improvements from rc1 through rc6.

### What's new since rc6

- **Cheat execution:** corrected data widths, register selection, immediate values, and pointer-chain offsets. These errors could prevent loaded cheats from taking effect.
- **Process-memory services:** wired `SetProcessMemoryPermission`, `MapProcessMemory`, and `UnmapProcessMemory` into both ARM64 and ARM32 system-call dispatch. Aligned permission handling and validation order with Eden, with tests for writable aliases, unmapping, and error handling. This addresses missing calls needed by injected cheat modules; end-to-end compatibility with third-party CheatVM modules is not yet verified.
- **Applet compatibility:** added Eden's success response for `ILibraryAppletAccessor` command 90. Also implemented `GetLibraryAppletInfo` to return the child applet's identity and mode.

releases.name: Ruzu v0.1.1-rc6
releases.body:
This release candidate fixes an audio-update parsing error that could cause invalid mixer data and audio glitches.

**This is a pre-release for testing before v0.1.1.** Feedback and reproducible bug reports are welcome. It includes all improvements from rc1 through rc5.

### What’s new since rc5

- **Audio update parsing:** the audio renderer now respects the splitter block size declared in the update header. Previously, it could read the following mixer block at the wrong offset, resulting in invalid mix counts or rejected audio updates.
- **Input validation:** added bounds checks for declared splitter blocks.
- **Regression coverage:** added synthetic tests covering splitter block boundaries, subsequent mixer updates, and header layout.

This correction addresses a likely cause of the audio errors reported in [issue #21](https://github.com/vricosti/ruzu-emu/issues/21). Confirmation through extended gameplay is still needed.

### Known limitations

Unsupported shader instructions may still cause missing graphics or prevent a scene from rendering. This release does not resolve every freeze, black-screen issue, or audio glitch.

releases.name: Ruzu v0.1.1-rc5
releases.body:
**This release candidate improves shader error handling, Windows build support, and diagnostics for freezes and black screens.

**This is a pre-release for testing before v0.1.1.** Feedback and reproducible bug reports are welcome. It includes the improvements from rc1 through rc4.

### What’s new since rc4

- **Shader stability:** unsupported shader instructions now produce an error that the Vulkan pipeline compiler can handle, rather than terminating the GPU worker. This improves error recovery but does not add support for those instructions.
- **Graphics compatibility:** aligned constant-buffer and texture validation with Eden and corrected how constant-buffer values are recorded for shader caching.
- **Windows memory handling:** aligned unsupported memory-protection handling with Eden, avoiding an unconditional panic.
- **Windows builds:** improved detection of existing Visual Studio installations and installation of missing C++ tools. Runtime DLLs are now copied alongside the build binaries, and a vcpkg compatibility fix was added.

releases.name: Ruzu v0.1.1-rc4
releases.body:
This release candidate adds support for multi-program titles such as game collections and fixes an ordering problem in kernel thread termination.

**This is a pre-release for testing before v0.1.1.** Feedback and reproducible bug reports are welcome. It includes the improvements from rc1, rc2 and rc3.

### What’s new since rc3

- **Game collections:** titles that chain into a sub-program (`ExecuteProgram`) now work. Previously, picking a game from a collection’s menu left the screen frozen at 0 FPS. Ruzu now shuts the running program down and boots the requested program of the same file. 
- **Kernel:** thread termination now signals completion and notifies waiting threads under the scheduler lock, after the terminating thread has left its core. This closes an ordering window between the two notifications.

### Known limitations

Only the collection listed above was tested with the new sub-program launch path. Other multi-program titles may still expose missing behavior, and reports are welcome.

### Downloads

On Windows, choose the installer or extract the standalone ZIP.

releases.name: Ryudeck v0.1.23
releases.body:
## v0.1.23 (2026-07-07)

> _Report anything that misbehaves._

**New — Mii selector & creator**
- In-game **"Create a Mii"** (Miitopia, and any title that calls the Switch Mii applet) now opens a
  real, gamepad-navigable Mii selector: pick one of your existing system Miis, generate a random
  Mii, or cancel — instead of the game being silently handed a blank default face. A random Mii is
  saved into your system Mii database, so games that re-read it pick it up too.
- Guest applet dialogs — the Mii selector, profile selection, and controller-connect prompts — now
  **render and are fully controller-drivable in Game Mode**. Previously, because a guest applet
  pauses the game, the emulator's frame loop went idle and the overlay never composited over the
  frozen frame (it showed as a black screen); it now re-composites the overlay over the held frame,
  so the menu appears over your game and the D-pad / A / B drive it, handing control back cleanly.
- **Direct Mii Creator access** from the launcher top bar — the full Mii editor is one button away,
  as befits a Switch headline feature.

**New — Deck-native input**

releases.name: Ryudeck v0.1.22
releases.body:
**New — Frame Generation (experimental)**
- **Frame Generation ships as an opt-in**: toggle it live in the Quick-Access blade (L3+R3) or per
  game in settings. It runs AMD FidelityFX optical-flow frame interpolation inside Ryudeck's own
  Vulkan present path — no external layers — presenting an interpolated frame between each pair of
  real frames on a dedicated present thread. GPU-light titles roughly double their perceived
  frame rate (measured on device: ~21-30 fps rendered → ~42-60 presented).
- It is self-limiting by design: generation only engages when it actually helps — it suspends below
  a per-title frame-rate floor, when the GPU has no spare headroom (measured from real per-frame GPU
  time, so misreported "100% busy" titles are handled), and when the game already runs near panel
  rate. A zero-delay dip veto skips generation for any single spiked frame (e.g. a shader-compile
  stall), so sudden hitches are never smeared into interpolated frames.
- Fixed: the feature now engages reliably on every launch (previously a first-launch state could
  latch process-wide), the blade reports its live state honestly (including a "restart game" hint

releases.name: Ryudeck v0.1.21
releases.body:
**Smoother in motion — every game**
- Fixed a per-frame Vulkan memory allocation in the FSR upscaler (the default scaler) that blocked the render thread on GPU fences hundreds of times per second under load. Heavy titles no longer dip as hard when the camera moves — every game running the FSR scaler benefits.

**New — console features**
- **Console Mode**: choose Docked or Handheld globally *and* per game, with a live mode tag in the overlay. Your per-game choice always outranks the built-in recommendation.
- **Cheats in the Quick-Access blade** (L3+R3): browse and toggle individual cheats live, in-game.
- **Boot lands on your last-played game**; launcher + overlays navigate with the left thumbstick too.
- Controller-aware button glyphs, a boot splash, gallery export, usage-based achievements, a real battery reading, and over-scroll fixed in every list.

**Stability — sessions survive more**
- **A GPU crash no longer kills your session** — the reset is contained and you're routed back to the launcher.
- **Closing from Steam now exits cleanly in seconds** (was an 8-second hang + force-kill, every time).

releases.name: Ryudeck v0.1.20
releases.body:
## v0.1.20 (2026-06-30)

**More games running**
- **Xenoblade Chronicles 3** no longer crashes on its fully-rendered opening cutscene. A shader the game
  compiles for one of its effects was producing SPIR-V the Steam Deck's AMD driver rejected (a hard GPU
  crash); it now plays through the cutscene into gameplay.
- **Super Smash Bros. Ultimate** now boots into gameplay — it was crashing on load — and holds ~60 fps.
- **Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu!** no longer soft-locks on the control-select screen: the game asks for a
  Handheld controller, which Ryudeck's per-game profile now binds automatically.
- **Luigi's Mansion 3** now boots into gameplay with its title update (a first; still rough).
- Fresh on-device compatibility captures added for Super Mario Odyssey, Super Mario Bros. Wonder, and

**Frame pacing — simpler + correct**
- The QAM **Frame Rate** control is now **two clear knobs** instead of three overlapping ones:
  **Frame Rate** (Native / 60 / Uncapped) and **Speed** (Normal / Turbo). "Decouple" is no longer

emulators.name: gears of war 2 pc port
emulators.description: 《战争机器 2》Xbox 360 版的静态重编译 PC 移植。
emulators.latest_body:
Phones get new defaults that run smoother and cooler, voices on Android should come through again, and every platform gets a Render scale option. Everything from [0.4.6](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.6) is included.

## Android

- **Frame rate unlocked with a 45 fps limit, by default.** Uncapped, the phone's GPU runs at full load until the phone lowers its clock as it heats up; the limit keeps headroom. The limit drops to the nearest rate that divides your screen's refresh, so every frame lasts the same: 40 fps on a 120 Hz screen (Galaxy S24/S25), 45 at 90 Hz, 30 at 60 Hz. On an S25 Ultra frame times went from a 25/25/16.7 ms mix to an even 25 ms. You can still pick 30, 60 or no limit in Device Options > Display > Frame rate limit.
- **Render scale 75 % by default.** The 3D scene is drawn at 75 % and scaled up to the screen; on an S25 Ultra that is 14 % less GPU work per frame, with a slightly softer picture. Graphics > Render scale goes back to 100 %.
- **Snapdragon GSR for the final upscale by default**, one pass instead of FSR 1's two.

## Android

- **Frame rate unlocked with a 45 fps limit, by default.** Uncapped, the phone's GPU runs at full load until the phone lowers its clock as it heats up; the limit keeps headroom. The limit drops to the nearest rate that divides your screen's refresh, so every frame lasts the same: 40 fps on a 120 Hz screen (Galaxy S24/S25), 45 at 90 Hz, 30 at 60 Hz. On an S25 Ultra frame times went from a 25/25/16.7 ms mix to an even 25 ms. You can still pick 30, 60 or no limit in Device Options > Display > Frame rate limit.
- **Render scale 75 % by default.** The 3D scene is drawn at 75 % and scaled up to the screen; on an S25 Ultra that is 14 % less GPU work per frame, with a slightly softer picture. Graphics > Render scale goes back to 100 %.
- **Snapdragon GSR for the final upscale by default**, one pass instead of FSR 1's two.

releases.name: v0.4.6
releases.body:
Insane can now be picked from the start. Everything from [0.4.5](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.5) is included; if you have not read its notes, they cover the Riftworm fix for Vulkan, GPU detection on Linux and Proton, and the co-op go-to-player-1 key.

## Every platform

- **Insane without finishing the campaign first.** The option from 0.4.5, now named **All chapters and Insane unlocked** (PC Options > Saves, on by default), also enables the Insane button in the difficulty menu, in solo Campaign and in the co-op lobby. Before, the game greyed it out until the campaign had been finished once. As with chapters, only the menu check changes: your saved progress and the Extras list of unlockables are not touched.

## Known, still open

- Lighting that looks pixelated on Linux with presets above Low, and black textures on Low on Windows (both on a Legion Go): we could not reproduce them on our PC. A screenshot and the `logs/gow2_*.log` of the run, with the chapter, help a lot.

releases.name: v0.4.5
releases.body:
The Riftworm interior no longer crashes or goes black with Vulkan, the game picks the right GPU settings on Linux and under Proton, every chapter can be picked from the start, and co-op gets a key and a controller combo to go to player 1. Everything from [0.4.4](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.4) is included.

## Vulkan (Linux and SteamOS, Proton with Vulkan, Android, Vulkan on Windows)

- **Inside the Riftworm (act 5) no longer loses the GPU.** The worm's flesh is drawn with tessellation, and the shaders the renderer builds for it read their settings from the wrong slot, so the tessellation factor came from unrelated memory: the scene stayed black, would not load, or the game closed with a lost device. Fixed in SDK patch 0091 (found with the Khronos validation layer). On a Radeon RX 7800 XT the worm interior now runs 120 s at 60 fps where it failed within seconds. Under Proton, Vulkan (`gpu_backend = vulkan`) is the backend to use for that chapter: D3D12 through vkd3d-proton was also reported to lose the device there and we could not test it.

## Linux and SteamOS

releases.name: v0.4.4
releases.body:
Less memory traffic on phone GPUs, less work per draw on the GPU command thread, and a new option for the CPU core the game spins while it waits for the GPU. Everything from [0.4.3](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.3) is included.

## Vulkan (Android, Linux and SteamOS, Vulkan on Windows)

- **Each render pass now covers only what it draws.** The renderer sizes its render targets for the console's whole EDRAM (1520x3456 on the phone) and every render pass loaded and stored all of it, even when its draws touched only the 1280x720 of a 720p frame. Phone GPUs render in tiles and pay for every byte a pass loads and stores, so they moved about 5.7 times the memory they needed. Now each pass begins with only the area its draws and clears can write (SDK patch 0089). It follows the Vulkan rules, so the picture should not change; it has not been measured on a phone yet. If part of the picture looks missing or stale, set `vulkan_tight_render_area = false` in `gow2.toml` (it takes effect at once) and open an issue with the scene. Direct3D 12, the Windows default, is not affected.

## Every platform

releases.name: v0.4.3
releases.body:
A new Android APK that survives leaving the game, a leaner game binary on every platform, and threads that sleep instead of polling on Linux and Android. Everything from [0.4.2](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.2) is included.

## Android

- **Leaving the game and coming back no longer crashes it.** Home, switching to another app or the screen turning off, then coming back: up to 0.3.18 the return crashed (in `vkCreateAndroidSurfaceKHR`, with a window Android had already freed). Now the game lets go of the old window when it leaves the screen and connects to the new one when it comes back (SDK patch 0085). The game keeps running while it is off screen (only the picture and the sound stop), so pause it before you leave.
- **The update dialog holds the game until you answer it**, instead of letting it start behind the dialog, and the phone only offers releases that carry an APK (0.4.2 was for PC and Linux only).

releases.name: ScummVM 2026.1.0: "Like a version"
releases.body:
Another year has gone by, therefore we are releasing a new ScummVM version. As you may notice right away, we are changing our version numbering schema, but that’s not all! We are also planning on more frequent releases!, which you can read about on [sev’s blog](https://www.patreon.com/posts/new-milestone-in-149535385).

This could be the biggest release we have made so far in terms of the added features and engines. If I count correctly, we have added 12 new engines to our compatibility page. Not games, engines. In terms of games, it is challenging to count, since two of the engines, SLUDGE and WAGE are authoring tools, but if you count games in our detection tables, that adds up to at least 194 titles!

And there is so much more...

# Changelog

releases.name: ScummVM 2.9.1: "Slappin da BASS"
releases.body:
Get ready to jam and slap da BASS!

Yes, it is this time of the year again! Please welcome the first ScummVM release of the year: ScummVM 2.9.1.

This maintenance release mainly focused on fixing bugs that our developers and users have uncovered since our last stable release.

## This is the first public beta release of **SeedlessDS**. SeedlessDS is a Nintendo DS emulator app for Android built around the **DraStic r2.6.0.4a** core, with a new Android frontend, a new UI written in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose, RetroAchievements integration work, and dual-screen behavior designed for modern Android handhelds.

emulators.latest_body:
# SeedlessDS 1.1 正式版

版本名为 `1.1`，版本号为 `153`。本次同时发布原包名替换版、共存版、对应源码及 SHA-256 校验文件。两版均关闭 Android 调试标志，正式版本号与发布文件名均不含 debug，测试控制面板关闭。

## 本次改进

- 修复后台存档提前完成时，完成状态被模拟线程覆盖，导致后续快速存档和读档一直被忽略的问题。
- 减少存读档结束后的多余槽位查询、成就附加档读取和目录扫描，成就校验改为流式 SHA-256。
- 拆分即时存档、游戏电池存档和其它文件的访问锁，避免后台慢存档连带阻塞游戏文件读取。后台存档线程降低优先级。
- 防止并发慢查询重新发布已失效的目录列表，修复日志时间格式化的并发访问。
- 在应用私有目录保留有大小上限的近期存读档记录，便于追查偶发卡顿。
- 保留 SoundTouch 原声音高加速、低延迟音频恢复修复，以及按 RP Duo 上下屏实际画面尺寸适配的柔和颗粒、柔和颗粒＋和 Nova 磷光点滤镜。

## 安装包选择

| 文件 | Android 包名 | 安装方式 |
|---|---|---|
| `seedless-ds-1.1-coexist.apk` | `com.seedlessds.app.debug` | 可直接更新本分支旧共存版，也可与官方版共存 |
| `seedless-ds-1.1-replacement.apk` | `com.seedlessds.app` | 原包名替换版 |
| `seedless-ds-fork-1.1-src.zip` | — | 两版对应的完整源码与构建配置 |
| `seedless-ds-1.1-SHA256.txt` | — | 安装包和源码校验值 |

共存版按用户选择保留历史包名中的 `.debug`，以支持覆盖更新，应用本身已关闭调试。两版均沿用本分支旧签名。

替换版与官方版签名不同。首次换用替换版，请先导出存档与配置，再卸载官方版并安装。直接覆盖官方版会因签名不匹配而失败。两个包名的数据各自独立，切换使用时需导入存档。

两版均支持 ARM64，最低 Android 5.0。证书 SHA-256 为 `99e2395bd7c458a577e6bc4f4c7237a7474cb20a178fad07313c2778a7943165`，沿用仓库随源公开测试签名。

## 验证范围

- 两种正式构建各 128 项应用测试通过，完成构建、Lint、包名和签名检查，并核对 `debuggable=false`、`testOnly=false` 及 `BuildConfig.DEBUG=false`。两版的应用资源和原生库一致。
- 原生回归覆盖 21 类存档故障、280 轮重复存读档及请求交错。

releases.body:
# 原声加速修复与 RP Duo 滤镜

加速时使用 SoundTouch 保留音高，音乐和音效节奏随游戏加快。修复此前加速连续爆音，以及 1.0.38 加速声音尖锐的问题。RP Duo 用户已确认 1.0.39“音色自然了，效果合适”。

包含按上下屏实际画面尺寸适配的 Vulkan 柔和颗粒、柔和颗粒＋和 Nova 磷光点滤镜，以及低延迟音频的暂停恢复和异常回退修复。

## 下载选择

| 文件后缀 | 用途 | Android 包名 |
|---|---|---|
| `replacement.apk` | 原包名替换版 | `com.seedlessds.app` |
| `coexist.apk` | 与官方版共存，可更新本分支旧共存版 | `com.seedlessds.app.debug` |

- 替换版与共存版各 115 项应用测试通过，34 项 AAudio 回归、9 项 OpenSL 队列回归通过。

- 两种安装包构建与包名、签名检查通过，替换版通过独立 Lint 检查。
- 共存版完成 RP Duo 用户听测确认。替换版尚未在掌机安装听测，所有游戏和长时间高倍率运行尚未逐项覆盖。

两版沿用本分支公开测试签名。证书 SHA-256 为 `99e2395bd7c458a577e6bc4f4c7237a7474cb20a178fad07313c2778a7943165`。
